mechanics.name: Rillaboom (base forme) species data and computed Lv50 stats
mechanics.behavior: Mod resolution: data/mods/champions/scripts.ts has no `inherit`, so its parent is base (sim/dex.ts:693); base is gen9, and data/mods/gen9 does not exist at this commit (sim/dex.ts:772-773). data/mods/champions has no pokedex.ts, so species data is base data. Rillaboom #812: types [Grass]; base stats 100/125/90/60/70/85; abilities {0: Overgrow, H: Grassy Surge}; weightkg 90 (weighthg 900); genderRatio M .875 / F .125. The set uses Grassy Surge. No ability-changing effect exists in either team, so Overgrow cannot be reached. Rillaboom-Gmax is isNonstandard Past in champions, so it cannot be reached. Champions tier is OU, so the species is legal. The champions learnset has Fake Out, Grassy Glide, High Horsepower and Wood Hammer as 9M. Set: Lv50 (Adjust Level = 50), Adamant (+Atk -SpA), stat points HP18/Atk32/Def2/SpA0/SpD6/Spe8 (66 total), IVs 31. Champions stats: HP 193, Atk 194, Def 112, SpA 72, SpD 96, Spe 113. No unmodified team member ties 113 Speed. Nearest are Ceruledge 106, Archaludon 114 and Gholdengo 118; full list: A = Staraptor 167 / Mega 178, Milotic 101, Ceruledge 106, Raichu 178 / Mega-Y 200, Gholdengo 118; B = Politoed 94, Golisopod 61, Archaludon 114, Farigiraf 80, Charizard 163 / Mega-Y 163, Grimmsnarl 72. Weight matters only for the opposing Grass Knot, which gets 80 BP (weighthg >= 500). Low Kick, Heat Crash and Heavy Slam are not in either team. Gender: the pokepaste has no gender line, and the validator leaves gender '' for species without a fixed gender. The Pokemon constructor then calls battle.sample(['M','F']), which is uniform and ignores genderRatio. No gender-dependent mechanic (Attract, Rivalry, Captivate) is in the closure.
mechanics.rng_draws: 1 PRNG draw (random(2) via sample) at Pokemon construction when set.gender is empty. The DuoForge fixture must either replicate this draw or pin the gender explicitly, and record which.

mechanics.name: Champions stat-point stat formula, validation, level
mechanics.behavior: set.evs holds Champions Stat Points. The format has no Level Clause Mod, so champions statModify uses HP = base + SP + 75 and every other stat = base + SP + 20. Nature applies as stat = trunc(trunc(stat*110, 16)/100) for the plus stat, or *90 for the minus stat. Level and IVs are ignored. Validator: each stat <= 32 SP; total <= 66 (evLimit Auto -> 66 for champions mods); all IVs must be 31. Flat Rules (champions) forces Adjust Level = 50. The level still feeds the damage formula: trunc(2*50/5+2) = 22. Rillaboom: HP 100+18+75 = 193; Atk (125+32+20 = 177) -> trunc(19470/100) = 194; Def 90+2+20 = 112; SpA (60+0+20 = 80) -> 72; SpD 70+6+20 = 96; Spe 85+8+20 = 113. The Champions HP formula leaves no maxhp/baseMaxhp difference to handle.
mechanics.rng_draws: none
mechanics.champions_override: The whole formula is a champions override (scripts.ts:10-40). The base formula (sim/battle.ts:2354-2372) is not used.
mechanics.uncertainty: none for PS parity

mechanics.name: Champions PP formula and PP deduction for Rillaboom's moves
mechanics.behavior: Champions init caps every move with pp > 20 at 20; none of Rillaboom's moves is affected. calculatePP = noPPBoosts ? pp : (pp/5 + 1)*4 and ignores ppUps. The constructor passes ppUps 3, which is irrelevant here. Max PP: Wood Hammer 15 -> 16; Grassy Glide 20 -> 20; Fake Out 10 -> 12; High Horsepower 10 -> 12. runMove deducts 1 PP (no Pressure in either team) after the BeforeMove event succeeds and before TryMove, Try, TryHit and accuracy. So a move blocked by Armor Tail or Protect, or one that misses, fails or hits an immune target, still costs PP. A move prevented by flinch, full paralysis, sleep, freeze or a confusion self-hit costs none. deductPP returning 0 prints 'cant ... nopp'. That case is unreachable for chosen moves because 0-PP moves are disabled in the request. Struggle is exempt (id check).
mechanics.rng_draws: none
mechanics.champions_override: calculatePP and the init PP cap are champions-specific (base: sim/battle.ts:2374-2379).

mechanics.name: Grassy Surge
mechanics.behavior: onStart(source) calls field.setTerrain('grassyterrain'). In gen >= 5, getCallback maps an ability's onStart to the onSwitchIn handler of the 'SwitchIn' fieldEvent. That event runs in runSwitch at battle start (leads), after a switch action, and after an end-of-turn replacement. runSwitch first speedSorts all actives and records speedOrder, then speedSorts the SwitchIn handlers by priority, then by speed minus a fractional speedOrder index. Grassy Surge has no onSwitchInPriority, so its priority is 0 and it runs before Grassy Seed (-1). setTerrain returns false (no message, no duration refresh) when grassyterrain is already up. Otherwise it creates the terrain state with source = Rillaboom and duration 5; the durationCallback's Terrain Extender check is absent in both teams. It then fires singleEvent FieldStart ('-fieldstart ... [from] ability: Grassy Surge') and eachEvent('TerrainChange') in speed order. No effect in either team suppresses, copies, swaps or replaces the ability: no Neutralizing Gas, Mold Breaker, Skill Swap, Trace, Gastro Acid, Entrainment or Worry Seed. The flags are {} (not breakable). The terrain outlives Rillaboom's faint or switch-out.
mechanics.rng_draws: runSwitch speedSort(allActive) uses prng.shuffle on exact speed ties (sim/battle.ts:429-463). With a fixed speedOrder, SwitchIn handlers of different Pokemon do not tie.
mechanics.champions_override: none
mechanics.uncertainty: none

mechanics.name: Grassy Terrain (set by Grassy Surge)
mechanics.behavior: Terrain condition, duration 5 (8 only with Terrain Extender, which is absent). (a) onBasePower (priority 6): a Grass-type move whose user is grounded gets chainModify 5325/4096. This covers Rillaboom's Wood Hammer and Grassy Glide and the opposing Farigiraf's Grass Knot. (b) Earthquake, Bulldoze and Magnitude are halved against grounded targets. No such move is in either team, so this branch cannot be reached. (c) onResidual (order 5, subOrder 2): each grounded, non-semi-invulnerable active heals baseMaxhp/16 (heal truncates, minimum 1; a full-HP target gets no heal and no message). Rillaboom heals 12. Flying types (Staraptor, Mega Staraptor, Charizard, Mega Charizard Y) are not grounded and are skipped. No semi-invulnerable moves exist in the closure. (d) Grassy Glide gets +1 priority. (e) Grassy Seed is consumed. (f) onFieldResidual (order 27, subOrder 7) decrements the duration; at 0 it prints '-fieldend'. This happens after the order-5 heals of the same turn. Duration counting: set at battle start or turn start, the terrain lives through 5 residuals. Set by a mid-turn switch-in, the current turn counts. Set by an end-of-turn replacement (after residuals), it covers the next 5 turns. isTerrain goes through effectiveTerrain and runEvent('TryTerrain'); no handlers exist in the closure. Neither team can remove or replace terrain, so it ends only by duration, and a new terrain requires Rillaboom to re-enter after expiry.
mechanics.rng_draws: No draws of its own. Its per-Pokemon residual heal handlers join the residual speedSort; two actives with identical effective speed that reach order 5 / priority 0 / subOrder 2 trigger prng.shuffle.
mechanics.champions_override: none (no grassyterrain override in data/mods/champions)
mechanics.uncertainty: none

mechanics.name: Miracle Seed
mechanics.behavior: onBasePower (priority 15): if move.type === 'Grass', chainModify 4915/4096. This applies to Wood Hammer and Grassy Glide, but not to Fake Out (Normal), High Horsepower (Ground) or Struggle ('???'). Miracle Seed (priority 15) runs before Grassy Terrain (priority 6) in the BasePower event. Effective BP: Wood Hammer 120 -> 144 (seed only) / 156 (terrain only) / 187 (both); Grassy Glide 55 -> 66 / 72 / 86. The item is not consumable. No item removal or suppression exists in the closure: no Knock Off, Trick, Switcheroo, Thief, Covet, Fling, Embargo, Magic Room, Klutz or Corrosive Gas. It is not a mega stone. mechanics.name: Wood Hammer
mechanics.behavior: accuracy 100, basePower 120, Physical, Grass, PP 15 -> 16 (champions), priority 0, flags {contact, protect, mirror, metronome}, recoil [33,100], target 'normal' (one adjacent foe or the adjacent ally, chosen by the player). It gets STAB 1.5, Miracle Seed and, while grounded in Grassy Terrain, the terrain boost. Recoil: after the champions hit loop, if move.totalDamage > 0 (the HP actually removed from the target, capped by its remaining HP), recoil = max(1, Math.round(totalDamage*33/100)), dealt by battle.damage with effect 'recoil' (which runs the Damage event). A miss, an immune target (none for Grass here), a Protect block, an Armor Tail block (only if priority were > 0, which Wood Hammer never has) or a fainted-ally target causes no recoil. The target's faint is processed (champions scripts.ts:546) before recoil is applied (552-554). The contact flag has no effect in this closure: neither team has Rough Skin, Iron Barbs, Rocky Helmet, Flame Body, Static or contact-punishing Protect variants. The protect flag makes Protect block it. No champions override.
mechanics.rng_draws: accuracy randomChance(acc',100) (drawn even at 100%; skipped only when No Guard makes accuracy true); crit randomChance(1,24); damage roll random(16); plus retarget samples if the chosen foe fainted. Recoil makes no draw.
mechanics.champions_override: PP 16 via the champions calculatePP. Recoil placement comes from the champions hitStepMoveHitLoop override (scripts.ts:552-554).
mechanics.uncertainty: none

mechanics.name: Recoil / Struggle recoil, self-KO and double-KO win attribution
mechanics.behavior: applyRecoilDamage: struggleRecoil -> clampIntRange(Math.round(baseMaxhp/4), 1) = 48 for Rillaboom, dealt by directDamage with effect 'strugglerecoil', which skips the Damage event. Otherwise recoil -> clampIntRange(Math.round(dmg*33/100), 1) via battle.damage. Then, if HP crossed from above maxhp/2 to at or below it, EmergencyExit runs on the user; Rillaboom has no such handler. Self-KO: pokemon.damage sets hp to 0 and calls faint(), which queues it. useMoveInner also calls battle.faint when hp is 0 (idempotent). Both last Pokemon fainting: the target's faint was processed earlier by faintMessages(false,false,!pokemon.hp), with checkWin=false while the user was alive. Rillaboom's recoil faint is processed by runMove's closing faintMessages(), and checkWin(faintData) then calls win(faintData.target.side) when every side has 0 Pokemon (gen > 4). So Rillaboom's side wins a Wood Hammer or Struggle recoil double-KO on both last Pokemon. If Rillaboom survives, runMove's closing checkWin() gives the win normally.
mechanics.rng_draws: none
mechanics.champions_override: Recoil is applied from the champions hitStepMoveHitLoop (scripts.ts:552-554); the base logic is identical in intent.
mechanics.uncertainty: The double-KO winner was derived by reading the code (faint-queue order plus checkWin). It needs a reference fixture: last Rillaboom Wood Hammer KOs the last foe and dies to recoil.

mechanics.name: Grassy Glide
mechanics.behavior: accuracy 100, basePower 55 (gen9 value; no champions override), Physical, Grass, PP 20 -> 20, base priority 0, flags {contact, protect, mirror, metronome}, target 'normal'. onModifyPriority returns priority + 1 if field.isTerrain('grassyterrain') and the user isGrounded(). Rillaboom is always grounded in this closure: not Flying; no Levitate, Air Balloon, Magnet Rise or Telekinesis; Gravity, Ingrain, Smack Down and Iron Ball are also absent. battle.getActionSpeed computes the priority through singleEvent('ModifyPriority') and then runEvent('ModifyPriority'); nothing in the closure answers the latter for Rillaboom. This happens at queue insertion (battle-queue.ts:275) and again for every pending action after each action when the next action is a move (gen >= 8, battle.ts:2919-2925), so the terrain state at every recomputation matters. For gen > 5, getActionSpeed writes action.move.priority; useMoveInner copies that into the executing move, where Armor Tail reads it (priority > 0.1). With STAB, Seed and terrain: effective BP 86. The +1 bracket is shared with Grimmsnarl's Prankster-boosted status moves and Ceruledge's Shadow Sneak, and resolved by speed; Trick Room does not change priority.
mechanics.rng_draws: accuracy (drawn even at 100%), crit 1/24, damage random(16). The getTarget inside getActionSpeed can make retarget draws (see rule-doubles-single-target-choice).
mechanics.champions_override: none (PP unchanged at 20)
mechanics.uncertainty: none

mechanics.name: Fake Out (champions)
mechanics.behavior: accuracy 100, basePower 40, Physical, Normal (no STAB for Rillaboom; no Grass boosts), priority +3, PP 10 -> 12, flags {contact, protect, mirror, metronome}, target 'normal', secondary {chance 100, volatileStatus 'flinch'}. The base onTry fails with '-fail' plus a hint if source.activeMoveActions > 1. The champions override (inherit) adds onDisableMove: if pokemon.activeMoveActions > 0, call disableMove('fakeout'). That disable is visible (disabled: true), not hidden. endTurn clears every moveSlot.disabled and then runs runEvent and singleEvent('DisableMove') per move slot for every active Pokemon. activeMoveActions is set to 0 in switchIn and incremented at the very start of runMove, before BeforeMove. Any executed move action therefore disables Fake Out from the next turn until Rillaboom leaves the field and re-enters. That includes an action lost to flinch, paralysis, sleep, freeze or confusion; one blocked by Armor Tail or Protect; a miss; and a Fake Out on the ally. Because no Dancer, Instruct or Encore exists, the base onTry-fail path cannot be reached in this closure, but it stays as a parity guard. A disabled Fake Out counts toward the Struggle condition. Ghost targets (allies Ceruledge, Gholdengo) are immune: the type-immunity step fails before accuracy, so there is no accuracy, crit, roll or flinch draw. Steel targets (Archaludon, Mega Golisopod) take 0.5x. Protect (+4) blocks it. Armor Tail blocks it when the target is Farigiraf or Farigiraf's ally.
mechanics.rng_draws: accuracy random(100) < 100 (always drawn when the target is not immune or No Guard-affected); crit randomChance(1,24); damage random(16); secondary random(100) drawn per hit target even though chance = 100 (battle-actions.ts:1343).
mechanics.champions_override: data/mods/champions/moves.ts:354-361 adds onDisableMove, which makes Fake Out non-selectable after the first move action of a stint. PP 12.
mechanics.uncertainty: none for PS parity. Real Pokemon Champions behavior is not verified; the PS mod is the reference.

mechanics.name: Flinch (inflicted by Fake Out; also receivable by Rillaboom)
mechanics.behavior: secondaries() rolls random(100) per secondary per surviving target. On success, moveHit applies volatileStatus 'flinch' through addVolatile (no immunities or TryAddVolatile handlers in the closure: no Inner Focus, Shield Dust or Steadfast; Covert Cloak is Past in champions). Flinch lasts 1 turn: onBeforeMove (priority 8) prints 'cant ... flinch', runs the Flinch event (no handlers) and returns false, so the target does not act and loses no PP. It works only if the target has not yet acted this turn; otherwise the volatile expires unused at that turn's residual, when fieldEvent decrements duration and calls end. It does not stop a switch or a Mega Evolution, because mega actions (order 104) run before moves. Rillaboom can itself be flinched by Golisopod's Iron Head (champions 20%; it acts before Rillaboom only under Trick Room or through Rillaboom's speed drops) or by ally Raichu's Fake Out aimed at it.
mechanics.rng_draws: No draw of its own; the 100% Fake Out secondary still consumes random(100).
mechanics.champions_override: Iron Head's flinch chance is 20 in champions (moves.ts:545-551, base 30 at data/moves.ts:9722-9736).
mechanics.uncertainty: none

mechanics.name: High Horsepower
mechanics.behavior: accuracy 95, basePower 95, Physical, Ground, PP 10 -> 12, priority 0, flags {contact, protect, mirror, metronome}, target 'normal', no secondary, no STAB, no Seed or terrain boost. Ground immunity uses runImmunity -> isGrounded(). Charizard, Mega Charizard Y, Staraptor and Mega Staraptor (all Flying) are immune: '-immune' is printed and no accuracy draw happens. With other targets the accuracy draw is randomChance(acc',100), where acc' = 95 adjusted by net stages as trunc(95*(3+n)/3) or trunc(95*3/(3-n)). Example: at -1 accuracy (Muddy Water) acc' = 71. The Accuracy event applies No Guard when Mega Raichu Y is the target (ally).

mechanics.name: PP exhaustion / Struggle
mechanics.behavior: getMoves marks a slot disabled if moveSlot.disabled is set or pp <= 0, and returns [] if no slot is usable. getMoveRequestData then offers only Struggle (target 'randomNormal', disabled false), and chooseMove pushes moveid 'struggle' with no target (a targetLoc is rejected for a non-choosable target type). Rillaboom reaches Struggle once Wood Hammer, Grassy Glide and High Horsepower are all at 0 PP (48 uses: 16 + 20 + 12) and Fake Out is at 0 PP or disabled by the champions onDisableMove. Switching out and in re-enables Fake Out only while it still has PP. Struggle: basePower 50, Physical, accuracy true (no accuracy draw), noPPBoosts, pp 1, not stored in moveSlots, PP deduction skipped. onModifyMove sets type '???', which gets no STAB, no Miracle Seed or terrain boost, is not immune to anything and is neutral against every type. Flags {contact, protect}, so Protect blocks it. Recoil = round(baseMaxhp/4) = 48 via directDamage 'strugglerecoil'. Target: always resolved randomly among live foes (getRandomTarget -> side.randomFoe -> sample); it never hits the ally.
mechanics.rng_draws: Target sample draws happen in several places: (1) queue insertion, because targetLoc is 0 (battle-queue.ts:268-271); (2) every getActionSpeed call, whose getTarget always takes getRandomTarget for randomNormal: the initial one and each gen >= 8 re-sort before Struggle executes (battle.ts:2644, 2919-2925); (3) runMove getTarget (battle-actions.ts:219). Each draw is 1 PRNG call even with a single live foe (prng.sample calls random(len)). Then crit randomChance(1,24) and damage random(16). No accuracy draw.
mechanics.champions_override: none for Struggle itself. Champions Fake Out disabling makes Struggle reachable while Fake Out still has PP.
mechanics.uncertainty: The exact number of target draws depends on how many speed recomputations happen before Struggle executes. This was derived from the code and must be confirmed with a PS trace fixture.

mechanics.name: Doubles targeting for Rillaboom's 'normal'-target moves (choice domain and retargeting)
mechanics.behavior: All four moves are target 'normal', which is a CHOOSABLE_TARGETS type. In doubles, chooseMove requires a non-zero targetLoc that validTargetLoc accepts: either foe slot (1, 2) or the ally's slot (negative, adjacent), never self. validTargetLoc does not check occupancy or faint state. Per active Rillaboom per turn, the domain is at most 4 moves x 3 targets (fewer when slots are disabled or at 0 PP), plus a switch to each unfainted benched Pokemon among the 4 brought, or else a single Struggle. At execution, getTarget handles fainted targets. A chosen foe that has fainted -> getRandomTarget -> side.randomFoe() samples among live foes (activePerHalf = 2 path). A chosen ally that has fainted -> the fainted ally is returned and not retargeted, so getMoveTargets returns [] and the move fails with '[notarget]' after PP was paid. No live foe -> it falls back to foe.active[0]; that Pokemon is fainted, so the move fails. getTarget is also called inside getActionSpeed, so retarget draws can happen there. RedirectTarget: the only redirector in the closure is ally Raichu's Lightning Rod, which is Electric-only; there is no Follow Me or Rage Powder. Rillaboom's moves are never redirected.
mechanics.rng_draws: A sample (1 draw) each time getTarget resolves a fainted-foe choice: at every getActionSpeed recomputation (battle.ts:2644) and in runMove (battle-actions.ts:219). No draw when the chosen target is alive or is a fainted ally.
mechanics.champions_override: none
mechanics.uncertainty: The count of retarget draws inside getActionSpeed recomputations needs trace confirmation.

mechanics.name: Damage calculation for Rillaboom's attacks (champions modifyDamage)
mechanics.behavior: getDamage: runImmunity; basePower; critRatio = move.critRatio (default 1, no ModifyCritRatio handlers in closure) -> crit = randomChance(1,24) (gen >= 7 table); CriticalHit event (no handlers); BasePower event (Seed 4915, Grassy Terrain 5325 for Grass moves); attack = Atk with boosts (a crit ignores negative Atk stages and positive Def stages), then the ModifyAtk and ModifyDef events (no handlers for Rillaboom's side); base = trunc(trunc(trunc(22*BP*A)/D)/50). Champions modifyDamage: +2; spread x0.75 (never: every Rillaboom move is single-target); WeatherModifyDamage (rain and sun change only Water and Fire, so nothing here); crit trunc(x1.5); randomizer trunc(trunc(d*(100-random(16)))/100); STAB x1.5 via modify for Grass moves only; type effectiveness by repeated x2 or trunc(/2); burn x0.5 (Physical, no Guts); ModifyDamage event (Reflect 2732/4096); result 0 -> 1; final trunc(d,16). Effectiveness (typechart not overridden in champions). Grass (Wood Hammer, Grassy Glide): Politoed 2; Golisopod 1; Mega Golisopod (Bug/Steel) 0.25; Archaludon 0.25; Farigiraf 1; Charizard / Mega Y 0.25; Grimmsnarl 1; allies Staraptor / Mega 0.5, Milotic 2, Ceruledge 0.5, Raichu / Mega Y 1, Gholdengo 0.5. Ground (High Horsepower): Politoed 1; Golisopod 0.5; Mega Golisopod 1; Archaludon 2; Farigiraf 1; Charizard 0; Grimmsnarl 1; allies Staraptor / Mega 0, Milotic 1, Ceruledge 2, Raichu 2, Gholdengo 2. Normal (Fake Out): Mega Golisopod and Archaludon 0.5; Ceruledge and Gholdengo 0; all others 1. '???' (Struggle): 1 against everything.
mechanics.rng_draws: crit randomChance(1,24), then random(16) damage roll, per damaged target (in that order, crit first)
mechanics.champions_override: The champions modifyDamage override (scripts.ts:196-312) keeps the gen 6+ order but reports 4x/0.25x in log messages (Math.min(typeMod,2)).
mechanics.uncertainty: none for these moves (single-target, no multihit, no Parental Bond)

mechanics.name: PRNG consumption order for a Rillaboom action
mechanics.behavior: Per Rillaboom move action, in order. (0) Retarget samples in getActionSpeed recomputations and at queue insertion, only when needed (for Struggle, always). (1) runMove getTarget retarget sample if needed; activeMoveActions++. (2) BeforeMove handlers by onBeforeMovePriority: slp 10 (no draw); frz 10 (champions: counter first, then randomChance(1,4) only if the counter has not expired); flinch 8 (no draw); confusion 3 (counter; then randomChance(33,100); a self-hit adds a random(16) roll); par 1 (champions randomChance(1,8)). (3) PP deducted. (4) TryMove (Armor Tail), Try (Fake Out onTry), TryHit (Protect): no draws. (5) Type immunity: no draw; an immune target skips the rest. (6) Accuracy randomChance(acc',100) unless accuracy is true: Struggle, or No Guard involving Mega Raichu Y. (7) getDamage: crit randomChance(1,24), then random(16). (8) Fake Out secondary random(100). (9) Recoil: no draw. Other Rillaboom-related draws: the gender sample at construction; runSwitch speed-tie shuffles; queue.sort shuffles on priority and speed ties at every gen >= 8 re-sort; residual handler shuffles on speed ties; statuses Rillaboom receives (champions sleep sample([2,3,3]); confusion duration random(2,6); receiving the secondary draws of opposing moves).
mechanics.rng_draws: see behavior; every randomChance/sample/shuffle step is one or more prng.random calls (a shuffle of k tied items makes k-1 calls)
mechanics.champions_override: The par, slp and frz draw rules are champions overrides.
mechanics.uncertainty: Draw order was derived from reading the code; a controlled-RNG differential trace against PS at this commit is required before certification.

mechanics.name: Action ordering around Rillaboom (priority, speed, Trick Room, Tailwind, dynamic re-sort)
mechanics.behavior: Queue order classes: switch 103 -> megaEvo 104 -> moves 200 -> residual 300. Moves sort by priority, then speed, then shuffle on ties. Brackets in this matchup: Protect +4; Fake Out +3; +1 for Grassy Glide in terrain, Prankster status moves (Grimmsnarl's Reflect, Light Screen, Parting Shot) and Shadow Sneak; 0 for the rest; Trick Room -7. Rillaboom's speed is getStat('spe'). Ally Staraptor's Tailwind gives chainModify(2) -> 226 for 4 turns. Paralysis halves it with floor after the other modifiers -> 56. The champions pokemon.getActionSpeed returns -speed under Trick Room (no 10000 - speed, no 13-bit trunc), which also reverses speed-ordered event handlers because pokemon.speed = getActionSpeed(). In gen >= 8, after every action whose successor is a move: updateSpeed, getActionSpeed for all queued actions, queue.sort(). So Mega Evolutions earlier in the turn (Mega Raichu Y 200, Mega Staraptor 178, Mega Charizard Y 163), a Trick Room or Tailwind set mid-turn, and a terrain change all affect Rillaboom's position among the remaining actions.
mechanics.rng_draws: prng.shuffle on exact (order, priority, speed) ties in queue.sort; possible under Tailwind, Trick Room or paralysis combinations
mechanics.champions_override: getActionSpeed override (scripts.ts:46-54): Trick Room negates speed instead of 10000 - speed.
mechanics.uncertainty: none for PS parity

mechanics.name: Team preview, switching, fainting and replacement for Rillaboom
mechanics.behavior: Team Preview plus Picked Team Size Auto -> bring 4 of 6 in doubles; Rillaboom may stay unbrought, lead, or sit in the back. Open Team Sheets reveals non-stat set information at preview. switchIn: resets activeTurns and activeMoveActions to 0 (so Fake Out is re-enabled at the next endTurn DisableMove), sets moveSlot.used = false, creates new ability and item states, then queues runSwitch; runSwitch fires Grassy Surge. mechanics.name: Mega Evolution action (Staraptor via Staraptite)
mechanics.behavior: canMegaEvo is computed once at Pokemon construction. The champions override returns item.megaStone[pokemon.baseSpecies.name] ('Staraptor' -> 'Staraptor-Mega'), else null, and ignores itemUser. The request exposes canMegaEvo only when the Pokemon is not move-locked. A choice 'move N mega' is rejected if !pokemon.canMegaEvo, or if another Pokemon on the same side already chose mega this turn (choice.mega). resolveAction puts a megaEvo action (order 104) before the move action (order 200), after switches (103). Mega therefore happens at the start of the turn, before Protect's +4 priority and regardless of later flinch, full paralysis, sleep or freeze. runMegaEvo does: formeChange(species, item, isPermanent=true), which updates details, sends '-mega', runs setAbility(Contrary, isFromFormeChange) (no SetAbility event; End(Intimidate) and Start(Contrary) have no handlers), and recomputes types, weight and stats. It then sets canMegaEvo = false on every Pokemon of the side (one Mega per side per battle; Team A's Raichunite Y becomes unusable) and runs AfterMega (no listener in this closure). After the action, the gen>=8 block runs updateSpeed, recomputes getActionSpeed for all queued actions and re-sorts, so 178 Spe applies to this turn's remaining order. The gen-7 reinsert branch does not apply. When all PP is exhausted, the request is locked to Struggle and side.chooseMove returns before the mega check, so Staraptor cannot Mega Evolve on a Struggle turn. There are no RNG draws, except that the re-sort can shuffle on ties.

mechanics.name: Intimidate
mechanics.behavior: onStart runs as the SwitchIn handler (gen>=5 getCallback maps onSwitchIn to onStart for abilities). It iterates pokemon.adjacentFoes(); in doubles (activePerHalf <= 2) this is every non-fainted foe. On the first foe it logs '-ability Intimidate boost'. For each foe: if the foe has a substitute volatile it logs '-immune', otherwise it calls boost({atk:-1}, foe, staraptor, null, isSecondary=true). Boost pipeline: the boost aborts if target hp is 0, the target is inactive, or (gen>5) the target's side has no foe Pokemon left. Then ChangeBoost, getCappedBoost and TryBoost run. At -6 Atk it still logs '-unboost ... 0' for an Ability effect with isSecondary. Then AfterEachBoost and AfterBoost run, and statsLoweredThisTurn is set. Trigger points reachable for this set: the lead switch-in at battle start, a voluntary switch-in (switch action order 103), and an end-of-turn replacement after a faint. Team A has no pivot moves. SwitchIn handlers across simultaneous switch-ins are ordered by speed, with ties pre-resolved once in runSwitch (speedSort of all actives, then speedOrder fractional offsets). Flags {} (not breakable). After Mega Evolution the ability is permanently Contrary and Intimidate never fires again. No RNG draws except the tie shuffle in runSwitch's speedSort.
interactions: No Team B ability or item reacts to Intimidate. Abilities: Drizzle, Emergency Exit, Tough Claws (Mega Golisopod), Stamina, Armor Tail, Blaze, Drought (Mega Charizard Y), Prankster. Items: Mystic Water, Golisopite, Leftovers, Sitrus Berry, Charizardite Y, Light Clay. The Intimidate reaction hooks at abilities.ts:1735, 2158, 3031, 3160, 3778, 4089 and items.ts:118-125 are unreachable

mechanics.behavior: Fighting, Physical, BP 120, accuracy 100, base pp 5 (8 in Champions), priority 0, target 'normal' (in doubles the same 3 choosable locations as 'any': either foe or the ally), flags contact/protect/mirror/metronome, self: {boosts: {def:-1, spd:-1}}, no champions override. After damage and runMoveEffects, the champions spreadMoveHit calls selfDrops once (move.selfDropped is set because it is not multihit). This happens before secondaries and before the DamagingHit event. selfDrops always draws battle.random(100) even though self.chance is undefined, then applies moveHit(source, source, self, isSelf=true), which calls battle.boost. Contrary (Mega) inverts this to +1 Def / +1 SpD. The self-drop only occurs if the target was actually hit: Protect NOT_FAIL, a miss or an immunity filters the target out. It still occurs when the hit KOs the target. STAB only after Mega. Stages persist until switch-out and carry across Mega Evolution.
mechanics.rng_draws: accuracy random(100), crit random(24), damage roll random(16), self-drop random(100) (unconditional)
interactions: Effectiveness vs Team B: Politoed 1x, Golisopod 0.5x, Mega Golisopod 1x, Archaludon 2x, Farigiraf (Normal/Psychic) 1x, Charizard 0.5x, Grimmsnarl (Dark/Fairy) 1x
Vs allies: Ceruledge and Gholdengo are immune (Ghost; hitStepTypeImmunity), so there is no self-drop and no damage; Rillaboom, Milotic and Raichu 1x
Stamina and Emergency Exit are triggered as for Brave Bird
Base forme: the -1 Def/-1 SpD raises damage from Golisopod/Grimmsnarl physical hits and from special moves

mechanics.name: Tailwind (move)
mechanics.behavior: Flying, Status, accuracy true, base pp 15 (16 in Champions), priority 0, target 'allySide' (no target choice; the choice must not include a target), flags snatch/metronome/wind, sideCondition 'tailwind', no champions override. Executed through tryMoveHit: Try, PrepareHit, TryHitSide, then moveHit -> runMoveEffects -> side.addSideCondition. There is no accuracy step and no RNG. If Tailwind is already active on the side, addSideCondition returns false (the condition has no onSideRestart), so the move logs '-fail'. PP is still deducted. It is not blocked by Protect (no protect flag). Armor Tail does not block it (priority 0, own side).
interactions: No Snatch, Wind Rider or Wind Power in the closure (the flags are inert)

mechanics.name: Tailwind side condition
mechanics.behavior: duration 4 (durationCallback returns 6 only with Persistent, which is unreachable). onSideStart logs '-sidestart'. onModifySpe returns chainModify(2) for every active Pokemon on that side (Pokemon events bubble to side handlers), which exactly doubles speed after boosts. Paralysis applies later (onModifySpePriority -101): floor(final*50/100). Residual handler onSideResidualOrder 26, onSideResidualSubOrder 5: fieldEvent('Residual') decrements duration and calls onSideEnd at 0. It is active for the rest of the turn it is set plus the next 3 turns, ending at the 4th residual. Because gen>=8 re-sorts the queue after every action, it immediately reorders the remaining actions that turn. Under Trick Room, champions getActionSpeed returns -speed, so Tailwind makes the side act later. Team A speeds under Tailwind: Staraptor 334, Mega Staraptor 356, Raichu 356 (tie with Mega Staraptor), Mega Raichu Y 400, Rillaboom 226, Milotic 202, Ceruledge 212, Gholdengo 236.
interactions: Reflect and Light Screen from Team B use the same side residual order 26 (subOrders 1 and 2), so they tick before Tailwind's subOrder 5 on their own side
Speed ties under Tailwind: Mega Staraptor 356 = Raichu 356

mechanics.name: Protect (with protect and stall volatiles)
mechanics.behavior: Normal, Status, accuracy true, champions pp 5 (8 in battle), priority +4, target 'self', flags noassist/failcopycat, stallingMove, volatileStatus 'protect'. onPrepareHit returns !!queue.willAct() && runEvent('StallMove'). It fails with no RNG if no move, switch, instaswitch or shift action remains in the queue, i.e. Staraptor is the last to act. The StallMove handler exists only while the 'stall' volatile is present: success = randomChance(1, counter), and on failure the stall volatile is deleted. The accuracy step is skipped (self-target Status gives accuracy true). On success, runMoveEffects adds volatile 'protect' (duration 1, logs '-singleturn') and onHit adds 'stall' (duration 2, counter 3). A later addVolatile('stall') calls onRestart: counter *= 3 up to counterMax 729, and duration resets to 2. The protect volatile's onTryHit (priority 3) blocks any move with the protect flag (checkMoveBypassesProtect: HitProtect has no reachable handler; Z/Max are unreachable). It logs '-activate move: Protect' and returns NOT_FAIL. The champions Unseen Fist override is irrelevant (no holder). The protect volatile expires at the end-of-turn residual. stall expires after 2 residual ticks, so skipping one turn resets the counter.
mechanics.rng_draws: randomChance(1, 3^k) only on consecutive use (stall volatile present), see rng-protect-stall
interactions: Blocks Team B damaging moves (single-target and per-target for spread Heat Wave, Muddy Water, Snarl) and Parting Shot (no pivot results) and Spirit Break
Does not block Trick Room, Reflect or Light Screen (no protect flag; not targeted at Staraptor)
Also blocks an ally's Fake Out or Zap Cannon aimed at Staraptor

mechanics.name: PP exhaustion and Struggle
mechanics.behavior: When every move slot has pp <= 0, getMoves returns [] and getMoveRequestData substitutes [{Struggle, target 'randomNormal'}] with lockedMove = 'struggle', so no canMegaEvo is offered. side.chooseMove pushes {move 'struggle'} with no target and no mega. Switching remains legal (not trapped). Struggle: BP 50, Physical, accuracy true (no accuracy RNG), pp 1 with noPPBoosts (it is never deducted because it is not in moveSlots; runMove allows it), flags contact/protect/..., onModifyMove sets type '???' and logs '-activate move: Struggle'. '???' gets no STAB and neutral effectiveness with no immunity, because typechart has no '???' entry. Recoil (struggleRecoil) = clampIntRange(Math.round(baseMaxhp/4), 1) = 48 for Staraptor in either forme, via directDamage, which bypasses Damage events. Target 'randomNormal' is always chosen randomly among live foes. Staraptor reaches Struggle after 48 uses (16+8+16+8). There is no Endless Battle Clause in Flat Rules; the hard turn limit is 1000.
mechanics.rng_draws: random-target sample at resolveAction (battle-queue.ts:268-269), again in every getActionSpeed recomputation (battle.ts:2644) and in runMove getTarget (battle-actions.ts:223); crit random(24); damage random(16)
mechanics.uncertainty: The count of hidden target samples per turn depends on how many queue re-sorts occur while Struggle is queued. A PS-parity RNG trace must replicate getActionSpeed's getTarget call exactly.

mechanics.name: Doubles target selection and retargeting for Brave Bird and Close Combat
mechanics.behavior: 'any' and 'normal' are choosable target types: in doubles a targetLoc is mandatory, and validTargetLoc accepts foe slots +1 and +2 and the ally slot, but not self. 'any' requires !isSelf; 'normal' requires adjacency, and all three are adjacent in doubles. Tailwind and Protect must not be given a target. At execution runMove calls getTarget: a live Pokemon at the chosen location is used (a replacement that switched into that slot counts). If the chosen location holds a fainted foe, getRandomTarget calls side.randomFoe(), which calls prng.sample over live foes and consumes a draw even for a 1-element list. If it holds a fainted ally, there is no retarget, getMoveTargets returns [], and the move fails with '[notarget]' after PP is spent. For single-target moves in doubles, getMoveTargets runs priorityEvent('RedirectTarget'). Lightning Rod (ally Raichu) only redirects Electric moves, so it never redirects Staraptor's moves. getActionSpeed also calls getTarget for every queued move action (battle.ts:2644), including during each gen>=8 re-sort, so a move aimed at a fainted foe can consume extra sample draws before it executes. Per-turn option count while active: Brave Bird x3 targets + Close Combat x3 + Tailwind + Protect = 8, doubled by the mega flag while canMegaEvo, plus switches to non-fainted bench members.
mechanics.rng_draws: prng.sample on retarget (per getTarget call when the chosen foe slot holds a fainted Pokemon)

mechanics.name: Action ordering for Staraptor (priority, speed, dynamic re-sort, Trick Room)
mechanics.behavior: Actions sort by order, then priority, then speed, then subOrder, with ties shuffled by prng.shuffle (speedSort). Protect is priority +4; the other moves are 0. Action speed is the champions getActionSpeed: getStat('spe') with boosts and ModifySpe (Tailwind x2, paralysis x0.5); under Trick Room it returns -speed, with no 10000-x and no 13-bit truncation. After every action, if the next queued action is a move, gen>=8 runs updateSpeed() on all actives, recomputes priority and speed for every queued action, and re-sorts. So Mega Evolution (167 -> 178), Tailwind and Trick Room set mid-turn affect the remaining actions that turn. getStat caps Spe at 10000 (unreachable). Relevant speeds: Staraptor 167, Mega 178, Charizard 163, Raichu 178, Mega Raichu Y 200.
mechanics.champions_override: getActionSpeed override (scripts.ts:45-54) removes the Trick Room underflow and the 13-bit truncation.

mechanics.name: Recoil KO and last-Pokemon double KO result
mechanics.behavior: In the champions hitStepMoveHitLoop, faintMessages(false, false, checkWin = !pokemon.hp) runs after the hit loop. The target's faint is processed, but no win check runs while Staraptor is still alive. Brave Bird recoil is applied afterwards, and Staraptor may faint. runMove's later faintMessages processes Staraptor's faint and calls checkWin(faintData = Staraptor's faint). If both sides now have 0 Pokemon left, gen>4 awards the win to faintData.target.side, i.e. Staraptor's side. A recoil self-KO with foes remaining queues a normal end-of-turn replacement.
mechanics.uncertainty: Derived from reading the PS control flow (the faint queue order is the target, then the attacker). There is no dedicated PS test for this in the checked-out test/sim at this commit, and it was not independently verified against Champions in-game behavior.

mechanics.name: Switch-out and switch-in state for Staraptor
mechanics.behavior: On switch-out, the champions clearVolatile resets all boost stages (Close Combat drops, Contrary gains, Muddy Water accuracy changes), restores moveSlots, sets ability = baseAbility (Intimidate before Mega, Contrary after), clears volatiles (protect, stall, flinch, confusion) and restores setSpecies(baseSpecies), so the Mega forme is kept. Major status (burn, paralysis, sleep, freeze) persists. The Tailwind side condition persists independently of which Pokemon is active. On switch-in, runSwitch speed-sorts all actives (tie shuffle), records speedOrder and fires the SwitchIn field event, which triggers Intimidate only for the non-Mega forme.

mechanics.behavior: damageTaken codes: 0 = neutral, 1 = 2x, 2 = 0.5x, 3 = immune; dual types combine additively in log2 (clamped to -6..6 in champions modifyDamage) and immunity is checked separately. Defensive, Normal/Flying: Electric, Ice and Rock 2x; Ghost and Ground immune; Grass and Bug 0.5x; Fighting 1x. Defensive, Fighting/Flying (Mega): Electric, Ice, Psychic, Fairy and Flying 2x; Ground immune; Bug 0.25x; Grass, Dark and Fighting 0.5x; Rock and Ghost 1x. Offensive, Flying: 2x vs Bug, Grass and Fighting; 0.5x vs Steel, Electric and Rock. Offensive, Fighting: 2x vs Normal, Steel, Dark, Ice and Rock; 0.5x vs Bug, Psychic, Fairy, Flying and Poison; immune: Ghost.

Incoming super-effective moves vs Mega: also Psychic (Farigiraf), Spirit Break (Grimmsnarl), Hurricane (Charizard)
Drill Run and High Horsepower (Ground): immune in both formes

mechanics.name: Accuracy roll for Brave Bird and Close Combat
mechanics.behavior: hitStepAccuracy: accuracy = ModifyAccuracy(move.accuracy). If not true: stage = clamp(user accuracy stage - target evasion stage, -6..6) after ModifyBoost; positive stages give trunc(acc*(3+b)/3), negative give trunc(acc*3/(3-b)). Then the Accuracy event runs, and randomChance(accuracy, 100) = random(100) < accuracy. A draw is consumed even at 100%. Reachable modifiers: Muddy Water's 30% accuracy -1 on base Staraptor gives 75%; on Mega (Contrary) it gives +1 and trunc(133), which always hits but still draws. There are no evasion boosts in the closure. No Guard (ally Mega Raichu Y) returns accuracy true when Staraptor targets that ally, so no draw. Protect (self-target Status gives accuracy true) and Tailwind (tryMoveHit path) never draw.
mechanics.rng_draws: 1 x random(100) per target per Brave Bird or Close Combat execution that reaches step 4 (after Protect, type and immunity checks)
mechanics.uncertainty: PS PRNG consumption is PS-specific. Parity only matters if DuoForge aims for draw-exact PS replay.

mechanics.name: Critical hit roll
mechanics.behavior: critRatio defaults to 1 (Move constructor), and ModifyCritRatio has no reachable handlers for Staraptor. Gen 9 critMult is [0,24,8,2,1], so randomChance(1,24) runs per target per damaging hit (Brave Bird, Close Combat, Struggle). This happens in getDamage before the BasePower event. A crit multiplies damage by 1.5 (champions modifyDamage, after the spread and weather modifiers, before the random roll). It ignores the attacker's negative offensive stage and the defender's positive defensive stage (e.g. Archaludon's Stamina Def boosts) and bypasses Reflect.
mechanics.rng_draws: random(24) per damaging hit

mechanics.name: Damage random factor
mechanics.behavior: Champions modifyDamage order: +2, spread 0.75 (not reachable for Staraptor's single-target moves), WeatherModifyDamage (no effect on Flying/Fighting), crit 1.5, randomizer tr(tr(base*(100-random(16)))/100) (16 outcomes, 85-100%), STAB 1.5 (ModifySTAB), type effectiveness doubling/halving with truncation, burn 0.5 for physical moves, ModifyDamage event (Reflect 2732/4096), bypassProtect 0.25 (unreachable), minimum 1, then 16-bit truncation. Base damage = tr(tr(tr(tr(2*50/5+2)*BP*Atk)/Def)/50), with the Atk and Def stages applied through calculateStat.
mechanics.rng_draws: random(16) per damaging hit

mechanics.name: Close Combat self-effect roll
mechanics.behavior: selfDrops draws secondaryRoll = battle.random(100) unconditionally when moveData.self.boosts exists and the move is not a secondary. self.chance is undefined for Close Combat, so the drop always applies, but the draw is still consumed. It happens after the damage roll and before any DamagingHit reactions (Stamina, Emergency Exit).
mechanics.rng_draws: 1 x random(100) per successful Close Combat hit

mechanics.name: Consecutive Protect success roll
mechanics.behavior: Only when the 'stall' volatile is present (Protect succeeded on the previous turn): randomChance(1, counter), with counter 3, 9, 27, 81, 243, 729 (capped). No draw on the first use, and none when Protect fails because Staraptor acts last (willAct short-circuits first). A failed roll deletes stall, so the next Protect has no roll.
mechanics.rng_draws: random(counter) on consecutive Protect uses

mechanics.name: Speed ties involving Staraptor
mechanics.behavior: speedSort groups equal comparator results and calls prng.shuffle on each tied group. This covers queue ordering (every sort and re-sort), runSwitch's all-actives sort (which fixes speedOrder for SwitchIn/Intimidate ordering) and fieldEvent/eachEvent handler ordering. Reachable ties: Mega Staraptor (178) with Raichu (Timid, 32 Spe, 178) on the same side, also under Tailwind (356/356) and Trick Room (-178/-178). Base Staraptor at 167 ties nothing in the closure (Charizard is 163). Equal-priority move actions and SwitchIn and residual handlers may shuffle.

mechanics.behavior: getRandomTarget in doubles (activePerHalf 2) for foe-targeting moves returns side.randomFoe() = prng.sample(live foes), which draws even for a 1-element array. It is reached for Struggle (randomNormal: at resolveAction when targetLoc is 0, in every getActionSpeed, and in runMove getTarget) and for Brave Bird or Close Combat aimed at a foe slot whose occupant has fainted. Tailwind and Protect resolve to self with no draw (getAtLoc(0) is undefined, so getRandomTarget returns pokemon for self/allySide).

mechanics.name: Grassy Terrain vs Staraptor (ungrounded)
mechanics.behavior: Rillaboom's Grassy Surge sets Grassy Terrain. isGrounded() returns false for a Flying-type (no Gravity, Ingrain, Smack Down or Iron Ball in the closure). Staraptor and Mega Staraptor therefore get no Grassy Terrain end-of-turn heal (onResidual requires isGrounded), and the terrain's Earthquake-halving and Grass boost do not involve Staraptor. Ground moves (Drill Run, High Horsepower) cannot hit it at all (type immunity).

mechanics.behavior: Grimmsnarl's Reflect (5 turns, 8 with Light Clay) has onAnyModifyDamage: if the target is on the Reflect side and the move is Physical, not a crit, and not infiltrating, the modifier is chainModify([2732,4096]) in doubles. This applies to Brave Bird, Close Combat and Struggle. Brave Bird recoil is based on the reduced damage actually dealt.

mechanics.name: Burn on Staraptor
mechanics.behavior: Reachable via Heat Wave (Charizard, 10% burn per target hit). A burned Staraptor's physical damage (Brave Bird, Close Combat, Struggle) is multiplied by 0.5 in champions modifyDamage (no Guts). Burn residual (order 10) deals baseMaxhp/16 = 12 HP per turn. Recoil is based on the reduced damage dealt.

mechanics.name: Paralysis on Staraptor
mechanics.behavior: Reachable only via an ally's Zap Cannon (Raichu; 50% accuracy, 100% paralysis, Electric 2x vs Staraptor). Speed: par onModifySpe (priority -101) applies finalModify, then floor(spe*50/100). Base 167 becomes 83, Mega 178 becomes 89, and under Tailwind 334 becomes 167 or 356 becomes 178. Champions overrides onBeforeMove: full paralysis with randomChance(1,8) (not 1/4).

mechanics.name: Other incoming status and volatiles reachable on Staraptor
mechanics.behavior: Flinch: Iron Head (Golisopod), 20% in Champions (base 30%), and an ally's Fake Out (100%, priority +3; champions onDisableMove after the first activeMoveAction). Flinch blocks the move but not an already-resolved Mega Evolution. Confusion: Hurricane (Charizard, 30%). Its duration is random(2,6); on each BeforeMove there is a randomChance(33,100) self-hit using getConfusionDamage(40 BP typeless, using Staraptor's own Atk and Def with stages, so Contrary Atk gains increase it). Freeze: Ice Beam (Politoed or ally Milotic, 10%). Champions frz lasts at most 3 turns with a 1/4 thaw roll. Sleep: an ally's Hypnosis (60%); champions slp duration is sample([2,3,3]). None of these originate from Staraptor's own set. Their full specs belong to the inflicting members' closures.

mechanics.behavior: The format '[Gen 9 Champions] VGC 2026 Reg M-C' (mod champions, doubles, Flat Rules + VGC Timer + Open Team Sheets) has no Level Clause Mod, so champions statModify uses its non-level branch. Ceruledge, Adamant: HP 75+31+75 = 181; Atk (125+7+20) = 152, *1.1 = 167; Def 80+24+20 = 124; SpA (60+0+20) = 80, *0.9 = 72; SpD 100+3+20 = 123; Spe 85+1+20 = 106. Stats are stored once at construction (spreadModify).

Spe 106 sets turn order within a priority bracket

mechanics.name: Flash Fire
mechanics.behavior: onTryHit(target, source, move): when target !== source and move.type === 'Fire' (the type after ModifyType, so Weather Ball in sun counts), it sets move.accuracy = true. It then calls addVolatile('flashfire'); if the volatile already exists it prints '-immune'. It returns null, which removes Ceruledge from the move's target list: no damage, no secondaries, no accuracy roll for that slot. TryHit is hit step 1, before type immunity (step 2) and accuracy (step 4). TryHit handlers are ordered by compareLeftToRightOrder, which does not shuffle. Protect's volatile onTryHit (priority 3) runs before Flash Fire (priority 0), so a protected Ceruledge does not absorb (confirmed empirically). spreadHit is set from the target count before TryHit, so when Heat Wave is absorbed the partner still takes the 0.75x spread modifier (confirmed: '[spread] p1a'). The ability has flags {breakable: 1}, but neither team has Mold Breaker or any move that ignores abilities, so it cannot be bypassed. Its onEnd removes the volatile. Fire sources that can reach Ceruledge: opposing Charizard's Heat Wave (allAdjacentFoes, 90% accuracy, 10% burn) and Weather Ball while sun is active (Mega Charizard Y Drought). Team A has no Fire move other than Ceruledge's own Bitter Blade, and a move cannot target its user.
interactions: Weather Ball becomes Fire in sun (absorbed) and Water in rain (2x on Ceruledge)
Burn immunity comes from Fire typing, not this ability

The modifier folds into the ModifyAtk event and is applied with battle.modify (4096-based rounding) when runEvent ends. For Ceruledge it applies only to Bitter Blade: Atk 167 -> x1.5 after the stage multiplier. It lasts until switch-out: the champions clearVolatile override resets volatiles = {}. It also ends through the ability's onEnd, but no ability-suppression effect is reachable. A second activation while the volatile exists prints -immune and does not stack.

mechanics.name: Grassy Seed
mechanics.behavior: The champions mod does not override it, so it is inherited and legal (isNonstandard null). It is consumed, giving +1 Def, whenever Grassy Terrain is active and one of two things happens. (b) A TerrainChange event fires while Ceruledge is active: setTerrain -> eachEvent('TerrainChange') across all actives, sorted by speed with tie shuffle. useItem prints -enditem, applies item.boosts {def: 1} via battle.boost with effect = item, sets lastItem, and clears item. JS Math.round rounds halves up, so 65 damage heals 33 (confirmed). battle.heal truncates, raises nonzero amounts <= 1 to 1, runs the TryHeal event, and returns false with no message when the user is fainted, inactive or at full HP. Otherwise it logs '-heal ... [from] drain'. The heal happens before faint messages and before DamagingHit (Stamina), AfterHit and Sitrus. No Liquid Ooze, Big Root or Heal Block exists in either team.

mechanics.name: Protect
mechanics.behavior: Status, target self, priority +4. PP: the champions override sets base 5, so max 8. It fails ('-fail') when no move/switch/instaswitch/shift action remains in the queue, or when the stall roll fails; PP is still spent. On success it adds volatile 'protect' (duration 1, '-singleturn') and then volatile 'stall'. While active, protect's onTryHit (priority 3) blocks any move with the protect flag through checkMoveBypassesProtect, logging '-activate ... move: Protect', and returns NOT_FAIL. Every Team B move that can target Ceruledge has the protect flag. Self, side and field moves are unaffected. Protect is resolved before Flash Fire. It does not stop Mega Evolution or foes' self and field moves (Trick Room, Reflect, Light Screen, Tailwind).

Fails if Ceruledge is the last to act
A failed Protect still costs PP

mechanics.name: Stall counter (Protect chain)
mechanics.behavior: 'stall' volatile: duration 2, counterMax 729. onStart sets counter = 3. onStallMove succeeds with randomChance(1, counter); on failure it deletes the stall volatile. onRestart, called when a successful Protect adds stall again, multiplies counter by 3 while below 729 and resets duration to 2. The duration counts down in the Residual fieldEvent, so an unused turn clears the chain at that turn's end. Success chances for consecutive Protects: 1, 1/3, 1/9, 1/27, ... down to 1/729. A Protect that fails because nobody else will act does not reach StallMove, so the counter is not reset by it; the volatile simply expires.
interactions: Protect only (no Detect, Endure or other stall moves on Ceruledge)
mechanics.rng_draws: random(counter) per consecutive Protect attempt

Struggle: 50 BP Physical, accuracy true (no accuracy draw), flags contact and protect, noPPBoosts, and no PP deduction (runMove skips the nopp failure for Struggle). onModifyMove sets type '???': no STAB, no type effectiveness or immunity, so it can hit Farigiraf. struggleRecoil: after damage (only if totalDamage > 0), directDamage of clampIntRange(Math.round(baseMaxhp/4), 1) = round(181/4) = 45, logged '[from] recoil'. It can trigger the user's EmergencyExit check, which does not apply to Ceruledge. The target is a random adjacent foe: resolveAction calls getRandomTarget -> side.randomFoe() -> sample, and getTarget re-samples for 'randomNormal' on every getActionSpeed recompute and again at runMove. Foes' Protect blocks it, with no recoil (confirmed).

Freeze, paralysis or sleep can still prevent it in BeforeMove

mechanics.name: Damage formula for Ceruledge's attacks (L50)
mechanics.behavior: getDamage: basePower -> ModifyCritRatio -> crit roll (critRatio 1 gives 1/24 in Gen 7+) -> CriticalHit event -> BasePower event. attack = calculateStat(atk, stage) with the crit ignoring negative stages, then ModifyAtk (Flash Fire). defense = calculateStat(def, stage) with the crit ignoring positive stages, then ModifyDef. base = tr(tr(tr(tr(2*50/5+2) * BP * A) / D) / 50). Champions modifyDamage then applies, in order: +2; spread 0.75 if spreadHit (never for Ceruledge's single-target moves); WeatherModifyDamage (sun Fire 1.5, rain Fire 0.5); crit tr(x1.5); randomizer tr(tr(d*(100-random(16)))/100); STAB modify 1.5 (Fire and Ghost moves both get it); type: x2 per SE step, tr(/2) per resisted step; burn halving (never, since Fire is immune to burn); ModifyDamage event (Reflect 2732/4096 in doubles when not a crit); if 0 then 1; tr(,16). battle.modify uses a 4096-based rounding chain. The champions modifyDamage is arithmetically identical to base. The only difference is extra count arguments on the -supereffective and -resisted log lines.
interactions: Stamina/Grassy Seed Def stages on either side
mechanics.rng_draws: crit random(24) before the BasePower event; roll random(16) after the weather/crit steps; plus tie shuffles among ModifyDamage handlers
mechanics.champions_override: modifyDamage overridden (data/mods/champions/scripts.ts:196-312); arithmetic is the same as base
mechanics.uncertainty: none

mechanics.name: Doubles target selection, retarget and command domain
mechanics.behavior: Ceruledge's command domain per turn: Bitter Blade and Shadow Sneak each need a target loc (targetTypeChoices 'normal'): foe slot 1, foe slot 2, or the adjacent ally (in doubles every other slot is adjacent). Self is rejected as an invalid target. Swords Dance and Protect take no target; giving one is rejected. Switch to any healthy benched picked member. A 'mega' or 'terastallize' modifier is always rejected. At execution, getTarget returns the chosen Pokemon if it is unfainted. If a chosen foe has fainted, getRandomTarget -> side.randomFoe() samples a living foe (one PRNG draw even with one candidate). If a chosen ally has fainted, there is no retarget and getMoveTargets returns [] -> notarget fail. The RedirectTarget event runs in doubles; the only redirector in either team is ally Lightning Rod (Electric only), so Ceruledge's moves are never redirected. getActionSpeed calls getTarget too, so a fainted chosen foe can cause extra sample draws during the Gen >= 8 mid-turn re-sort. The ally's No Guard (Raichu-Mega-Y) makes Ceruledge's attacks on it skip the accuracy draw.

Ghost immunity to ally Fake Out and Close Combat

In Gen >= 8, after each action the sim runs updateSpeed() and getActionSpeed on all queued actions, then re-sorts the queue.

mechanics.name: PRNG draw sequence contributed by Ceruledge
mechanics.behavior: All draws come from battle.prng: random(n) = floor(next*n/2^32); randomChance(p,q) = random(q) < p; sample = random(len); shuffle is Fisher-Yates using random(start,end). Draws tied to Ceruledge's set: (1) gender sample at construction; (2) each damaging move per surviving target: accuracy random(100), then crit random(24), then damage roll random(16), then tie shuffles inside the ModifyDamage runEvent; no secondary roll (neither attack has secondaries); (3) Protect: random(counter) only while the stall volatile exists; (4) Swords Dance: none; (5) Struggle: sample(foes) at resolve, at each getActionSpeed recompute and at execution, then crit and roll; (6) retargeting after a chosen foe faints: sample(foes); (7) speed ties: shuffle in queue sort, the Gen >= 8 re-sort, SwitchIn/Residual fieldEvent and eachEvent. Flash Fire absorption, type immunity and Armor Tail stop the per-target draws for that target. No Guard (ally Mega Raichu Y as target) removes the accuracy draw.

Whether DuoForge copies Showdown's exact draw stream (including draws that decide nothing, such as sample on a single candidate) is a DECISION_CONTRACT question, not a rules fact.

mechanics.name: runEvent handler speed-tie shuffle (e.g. Reflect+Light Screen)
mechanics.behavior: runEvent sorts handlers with speedSort except for Invulnerability, TryHit, DamagingHit and EntryHazard, which use a fixed left-to-right order, and fastExit events. Handlers that tie exactly on order, priority, speed and subOrder are shuffled with a PRNG draw even when only one of them will act. Observed: with both Reflect and Light Screen up on Team B, every ModifyDamage event, including Ceruledge's Bitter Blade and foes' attacks into Ceruledge, used an extra random(0,2) draw after the damage roll.
interactions: Any pair of tied onAny/onSide handlers in the same event

mechanics.name: Milotic (Team A set: Sitrus Berry / Competitive / Calm / 32 HP, 29 Def, 5 SpD)
mechanics.behavior: Species data comes from the base Pokedex because the champions mod has no pokedex.ts. Type is pure Water. Base stats are 95/60/79/100/125/81 (HP/Atk/Def/SpA/SpD/Spe). Ability slots are {0: Marvel Scale, 1: Competitive, H: Cute Charm}, and this set uses slot 1, Competitive. Weight is 162 kg, stored as weighthg = weightkg*10 = 1620. There are no otherFormes, so Milotic has no Mega, Primal or other battle forme. It is legal in Reg M-C: champions formats-data gives tier 'UU' with no isNonstandard. The champions learnset lists all four moves as '9M' (coil, hypnosis, icebeam, muddywater). Final level-50 stats, confirmed by probe: HP 202, Atk 72, Def 128, SpA 120, SpD 165, Spe 101. The Calm nature raises SpD and lowers Atk. Grounded: it is not Flying, has no Levitate and no Air Balloon. Its weakness/resistance profile comes from the Water row of the type chart: weak to Electric and Grass; resists Fire, Water, Ice and Steel.
mechanics.uncertainty: The Champions species data is the base gen9 entry (no override exists). Whether cartridge Champions uses different Milotic data is not verifiable from the pin.

mechanics.name: Champions stat-point formula applied to Milotic
mechanics.behavior: The format [Gen 9 Champions] VGC 2026 Reg M-C uses mod 'champions', game type doubles, and the ruleset Flat Rules + VGC Timer + Open Team Sheets. It does not include Level Clause Mod, so the champions statModify takes its non-level branch. HP = base + SP + 75. Every other stat = base + SP + 20, then the nature is applied with 16-bit truncation: plus = tr(tr(stat*110,16)/100), minus = tr(tr(stat*90,16)/100). IVs do not enter this formula, and the validator requires all IVs to be 31. Stat points are capped at 32 per stat and 66 in total (evLimit 66 for champions mods). Level is 50 through Adjust Level = 50 (pokemon.ts:337). For Milotic: HP = 95+32+75 = 202. Atk = 60+0+20 = 80, times 0.9 = 72. Def = 79+29+20 = 128. SpA = 100+0+20 = 120. SpD = 125+5+20 = 150, times 1.1 = 165. Spe = 81+0+20 = 101. Stat points total 66. The damage formula uses level 50, so its level factor is tr(2*50/5+2) = 22.
mechanics.champions_override: statModify is fully replaced by data/mods/champions/scripts.ts:10-40 (the base formula is sim/battle.ts:2354-2372).
mechanics.uncertainty: Confirmed empirically: a probe built with the pinned sim printed maxhp 202 and stored {atk:72, def:128, spa:120, spd:165, spe:101}.

mechanics.name: Milotic has no Mega or Tera option
mechanics.behavior: Milotic holds Sitrus Berry, which has no megaStone field, and the Milotic Pokedex entry has no otherFormes. The champions canMegaEvo returns item.megaStone?.[species.name] || null, so it returns null. The Mega Rayquaza branch needs gen<=7 or the +past/+future tags and does not apply. canMegaEvo is set on the Pokemon at pokemon.ts:490, so the request never offers mega for Milotic. canTerastallize always returns null in champions. Milotic therefore never changes forme, ability, type or stats. Other Pokemon's Megas still affect Milotic: mega actions run at order 104, before all moves (order 200), so Milotic's moves that turn already see the Mega forme. Relevant cases: Charizard-Mega-Y (Fire/Flying, Drought, Spe 163) sets sun. Golisopod-Mega (Bug/Steel, Tough Claws) loses Emergency Exit and changes Muddy Water from resisted to neutral. Ally Raichu-Mega-Y has No Guard. Ally Staraptor-Mega has Contrary.
