mechanics.name: Competitive
mechanics.behavior: The handler is onAfterEachBoost(boost, target, source, effect). It returns early if there is no source or if target.isAlly(source), which covers self-inflicted and ally-inflicted drops. If any stat in the boost is negative, it calls this.boost({spa:+2}, target, target, null, false, isSelf=true). Battle.boost fires AfterEachBoost once per stat, inside the per-stat loop, and only when that stat actually changed (boostBy != 0). So Competitive triggers once for each lowered stat and never when the stat was already at -6. The +2 is capped at +6. The log shows '-ability|Competitive|boost' followed by '-boost spa 2'. Triggers reachable from Team B: Snarl (100% SpA -1, spread, sound, bypasssub), for a net SpA of +1. Spirit Break (100% SpA -1), net +1. Parting Shot (Atk -1 and SpA -1 in one boost call), which triggers twice for net Atk -1 and SpA +3. Farigiraf's Psychic (10% SpD -1), which gives +2 SpA. Politoed's Muddy Water (30% accuracy -1), which gives +2 SpA. Not reachable: Intimidate, because only Team A has it and Staraptor's Intimidate hits foes. Team A cannot lower Milotic's stats in a way that triggers it, since ally drops are excluded. Boosts gained this way are cleared on switch-out.
mechanics.champions_override: None: competitive is absent from data/mods/champions/abilities.ts.
mechanics.rng_draws: none of its own (the triggering secondary rolls belong to the foe's move)
mechanics.uncertainty: Confirmed by probe. Parting Shot gave the log sequence unboost atk 1, Competitive +2 spa, unboost spa 1, Competitive +2 spa, ending at boosts atk -1 / spa +3. Snarl gave a net spa of +1. A Snarl hit at spa -6 produced no unboost and no Competitive trigger.

mechanics.name: Sitrus Berry
mechanics.behavior: onUpdate: if hp <= maxhp/2, which for Milotic means hp <= 101, it calls pokemon.eatItem(). eatItem needs the holder active, with an item and hp > 0. It runs UseItem and then TryEatItem. Sitrus's onTryEatItem runs TryHeal with baseMaxhp/4. onEat calls heal(baseMaxhp/4). Battle.heal truncates, so 50.5 becomes 50. The berry is then consumed: item='' , lastItem set, ateBerry true, usedItemThisTurn true. Update runs through eachEvent('Update'), which champions hitStepMoveHitLoop calls after each hit and again after the hit loop. That means Sitrus can activate in the middle of a move, after damage is dealt and before the attacker's later effects. It also activates after Struggle recoil and residual damage. Nothing in either team blocks it: no Unnerve/As One, Heal Block, Knock Off, Trick, Bug Bite/Pluck, Incinerate, Magic Room or Embargo. It cannot activate at full HP or when heal would do nothing (hp >= maxhp returns false). Sitrus has no megaStone, so it does not affect Mega eligibility.
mechanics.champions_override: None: sitrusberry is absent from data/mods/champions/items.ts.
mechanics.rng_draws: none (but eachEvent('Update') speed-sorts actives; equal speeds consume prng.shuffle draws)
mechanics.uncertainty: Confirmed by probe. After Psychic, Milotic went 57/202, ate the berry and healed to 107/202 (+50).

mechanics.name: Muddy Water
mechanics.behavior: Special Water move. BP 90, accuracy 85, priority 0, critRatio 1. Base PP 10 becomes 12 in Champions. Target is allAdjacentFoes, so no target is chosen and Milotic's ally is never hit. Flags are protect, mirror, nonsky and metronome; nonsky, mirror and metronome do nothing in these teams. Secondary: a 30% chance of accuracy -1, rolled separately per target. The champions mod has no override for it. Order of events: getMoveTargets returns all living adjacent foes. spreadHit is set when there is more than one target at the start of trySpreadMoveHit, so the 0.75 spread modifier still applies to the remaining foe if the other one Protects or misses (probe-verified: Politoed protected, and Farigiraf alone still got spreadHit=true). If only one foe is alive, there is no spread modifier. The hit steps are: TryHit (Protect blocks), then type immunity, then accuracy per target. Each accuracy check is randomChance(acc,100) with acc = trunc(85*(3+b)/3) for b>0 or trunc(85*3/(3-b)) for b<0, where b = user accuracy stage minus target evasion stage, clamped to ±6. After that, each hit target gets a damage calc, then secondaries for each damaged target. STAB is 1.5. Rain gives 1.5x and sun 0.5x through WeatherModifyDamage, applied after the spread modifier and before the crit. The secondary boost is applied as isSecondary, so it is silent if the target is already at -6.
mechanics.champions_override: The move is not overridden. PP comes from champions calculatePP ((10/5+1)*4 = 12), and the damage modifier chain comes from champions modifyDamage, which is arithmetically identical to base and differs only in the -supereffective/-resisted log args.
mechanics.rng_draws: Per use with 2 living foes, in probe-verified order: (a) targeting sample draws, random(nFoes), several per turn (see rng-target-resolution-nontargeted); (b) accuracy random(100) per non-protected target, in target order; (c) per target that was hit: crit random(24), then damage roll random(16); (d) per damaged target: secondary random(100), even though the chance is 30 and even if the target fainted. Coil's +1 accuracy makes the check 113 but still consumes the draw.
mechanics.uncertainty: The empirical RNG trace for one Muddy Water into two unprotected foes was 6 targeting draws, 2 accuracy, crit/roll ×2 and 2 secondary draws.

mechanics.name: Coil
mechanics.behavior: Status move of Poison type. Accuracy true, priority 0. Base PP 20 stays 20 in Champions. Target is self, flags are snatch and metronome (Snatch is not present in either team), and it has no protect flag, so Protect cannot block it. Effect: boosts {atk:+1, def:+1, accuracy:+1} applied through runMoveEffects to Battle.boost. It never makes an accuracy roll: a self-target Status move is forced to accuracy=true in hitStepAccuracy. Stages are capped at ±6. When all three are already +6, boost() logs '-boost <stat> 0' three times and the move counts as failed (probe: moveLastTurnResult false). If only some stats are capped, it still succeeds. What the boosts do for this set: the accuracy stage raises Hypnosis accuracy (60 becomes 80 at +1, 100 at +2, 120 at +3) and Muddy Water accuracy (85 becomes 113 at +1). The Def stage reduces physical damage taken. The Atk stage only matters for Struggle, Milotic's only physical attack. All stages reset on switch-out.
mechanics.rng_draws: none (probe-verified: zero PRNG calls attributable to Coil; getTarget for 'self' returns the user without sampling)
mechanics.uncertainty: The +6/+6/+6 failure path was confirmed by probe.

mechanics.name: Ice Beam
mechanics.behavior: Special Ice move. BP 90, accuracy 100, priority 0, critRatio 1. Base PP 10 becomes 12. Target class is normal, so the player must choose one of the two foes or the adjacent ally. Flags are protect, mirror and metronome. Secondary: 10% freeze (status 'frz'). No STAB, since Milotic is Water. A check at accuracy 100 still calls randomChance(100,100), which consumes one draw. The only exception is when No Guard makes the accuracy true, which happens if the target is ally Raichu-Mega-Y. The freeze goes through trySetStatus. It silently fails if the target already has any status, if the target is Ice type (typechart ice frz:3; no Ice types are in either team), or in harsh sun (sunnyday onImmunity returns false for frz while the defender's effectiveWeather is sunnyday; probe-verified with Charizard-Mega-Y Drought). It also fails on a fainted target, although the secondary roll is still drawn. Fire types can be frozen, because only Ice has frz immunity in the type chart. Target resolution: if the chosen foe has fainted, getTarget and getMoveTargets retarget randomly among living foes (a sample draw). If the chosen ally has fainted, there is no retarget and the move fails with [notarget]. No RedirectTarget effect exists for Ice-type moves in these teams.
mechanics.champions_override: The move is not overridden (PP 12 via calculatePP). The freeze status it inflicts is the champions frz override, see status-frz-champions.
mechanics.rng_draws: Per use against a living, unprotected, explicitly chosen target: accuracy random(100), crit random(24), roll random(16), secondary random(100). That is 4 draws, confirmed by probe. Retargeting from a fainted foe adds a random(nFoes) sample draw at every getTarget call.
mechanics.uncertainty: The accuracy-100 draw and the sun freeze immunity were both confirmed by probe.

mechanics.name: Hypnosis
mechanics.behavior: Status move of Psychic type. Accuracy 60, priority 0. Base PP 20 stays 20. Target class is normal, so the player chooses a foe or the ally. Flags are protect, reflectable, mirror and metronome; reflectable does nothing here because neither team has Magic Coat or Magic Bounce. It sets status 'slp'. As a Status move it has ignoreImmunity=true, so the Psychic-type immunity of Dark types does not apply: it hits Dark/Fairy Grimmsnarl (probe-verified). It is not Prankster-boosted, so the Prankster Dark immunity does not apply either. Pipeline order: TryHit (Protect blocks; ally Gholdengo's Good as Gold returns null, giving '-immune' with no accuracy draw, probe-verified), then accuracy randomChance(acc,100) with acc modified by the user's accuracy stage and the target's evasion stage, then trySetStatus. If the target already has any status, the move fails with '-fail <source>' AFTER the accuracy draw. No terrain, Safeguard, Sweet Veil, Insomnia, Vital Spirit or Misty/Electric Terrain source exists in either team. The format has no Sleep Clause Mod: Flat Rules, VGC Timer and Open Team Sheets do not include it (probe: ruleTable.has('sleepclausemod') is false). Armor Tail does not apply because the move's priority is 0.
mechanics.champions_override: The move is not overridden. The sleep it inflicts uses the champions slp onStart (see status-slp-champions).
mechanics.rng_draws: accuracy random(100), then random(3) through sample([2,3,3]) when sleep is applied. Probe-verified.
mechanics.uncertainty: The failure against an already-statused target was confirmed by probe (the log shows '|-fail|p1a: Milotic' with [still]).

mechanics.name: Sleep (Champions duration)
mechanics.behavior: onStart logs '-status slp [from] move: Hypnosis'. It sets startTime = sample([2,3,3]), so a draw is consumed only when the status is actually applied, and sets time = startTime. The inherited base onBeforeMove (priority 10) decrements time on each attempt to move, adding one extra decrement for Early Bird (absent here). When time <= 0 it cures and the Pokemon acts in that same turn. Otherwise it logs 'cant slp' and returns false. No move in these teams is sleepUsable. In effect: with probability 1/3 the Pokemon loses 1 action (startTime 2), and with probability 2/3 it loses 2 actions (startTime 3). A blocked BeforeMove happens before PP deduction, so a sleeping Pokemon loses no PP. The counter lives in statusState, which persists through switching; the pinned sim has no gen9 reset. Status is cleared only by waking or by cure effects, and neither team has cure effects.
mechanics.champions_override: onStart duration replaced: base random(2,5) became champions sample([2,3,3]).
mechanics.rng_draws: one random(3) at infliction; none in BeforeMove
mechanics.uncertainty: Probe: Hypnosis on Grimmsnarl drew random(3)=1, giving startTime 3.

mechanics.name: Freeze (Champions duration)
mechanics.behavior: onStart sets startTime = time = 3 without drawing. Champions onBeforeMove: a move with the defrost flag bypasses the freeze, but no move in Team B has that flag (flag scan). Otherwise time is decremented; if time <= 0 the Pokemon thaws, otherwise randomChance(1,4) decides. On a thaw it cures and acts that turn. Otherwise it logs 'cant frz' and returns false. The effect is at most 2 lost actions: the 1st and 2nd attempts each thaw with probability 1/4, and the 3rd always thaws. The draw is short-circuited, so no draw happens when time reaches 0. Inherited base handlers still apply: onModifyMove for defrost moves; onAfterMoveSecondary thaws on thawsTarget; onDamagingHit cures when hit by a damaging Fire move other than Polar Flare. Reachable Fire hits on a Team B Pokemon frozen by Milotic come from Team A only, from Ceruledge's Bitter Blade. Team B's Heat Wave and sun Weather Ball only target Team A. Sun prevents new freezes but does not thaw an existing one in this code.
mechanics.champions_override: onStart and onBeforeMove replaced: base thaw was a flat 1/5 per attempt with no cap; Champions uses 1/4 per attempt with a hard 3-attempt cap.
mechanics.rng_draws: randomChance(1,4), i.e. random(4), on BeforeMove attempts 1 and 2 only
mechanics.uncertainty: Probe: attempt 1 drew random(4)=1 and stayed frozen (time 2); attempt 2 drew random(4)=0 and thawed. The Bitter Blade thaw is inferred from code and was not probed.

mechanics.name: Champions PP for Milotic's moves
mechanics.behavior: At init, Champions caps any move PP above 20 to 20; none of Milotic's moves are affected. calculatePP ignores ppUps and returns noPPBoosts ? pp : (pp/5+1)*4. That gives Muddy Water 12, Coil 20, Ice Beam 12 and Hypnosis 20, for 64 total uses (probe-verified). deductPP takes 1 per use. It runs in runMove after BeforeMove succeeds and before useMove, so it applies even if the move then fails or has no target, but not when Milotic is asleep, frozen or fully paralyzed. Pressure is absent from both teams. A move slot with pp <= 0 is disabled in the request.
mechanics.champions_override: calculatePP replaced (base is pp*(5+ppUps)/5).

mechanics.name: Struggle (PP exhaustion)
mechanics.behavior: When getMoves finds no usable move, getMoveRequestData offers only Struggle (target randomNormal), and chooseMove forces moveid 'struggle' regardless of input (probe: 'move 1' became struggle). Struggle data: Physical, BP 50, accuracy true (no accuracy draw), priority 0. Flags are contact and protect, among others. onModifyMove sets its type to '???', which means no STAB and neutral effectiveness against everything, Ghosts included. It deducts no PP. It uses Milotic's Atk 72, so Coil's Atk stages apply. Recoil is struggleRecoil = clamp(round(baseMaxhp/4), 1) = round(50.5) = 51. The recoil goes through directDamage and is not modified by any effect (probe: 202 went to 151). After the recoil, Sitrus can trigger on the next Update. The target is random among living foes, so it gets the same repeated targeting draws as Muddy Water.
mechanics.rng_draws: targeting samples (6 in the probe turn), then crit random(24) and roll random(16); no accuracy draw
mechanics.uncertainty: Recoil 51 and the draw sequence were confirmed by probe.

mechanics.name: Hidden targeting draws for non-chosen-target moves (Muddy Water, Struggle) and fainted-target retargets
mechanics.behavior: This is a Showdown implementation behavior that DuoForge must reproduce for RNG parity. (1) BattleQueue.resolveAction: when a move action has no targetLoc (Muddy Water and Coil have targetLoc 0), it calls getRandomTarget and stores getLocOf(result) as targetLoc. For allAdjacentFoes and randomNormal in doubles, this is side.randomFoe(), a sample over living foes that makes one random(n) call even when n = 1. (2) resolveAction then calls getActionSpeed, which calls getTarget(pokemon, move, targetLoc). validTargetLoc returns false for 'allAdjacentFoes', and randomNormal is excluded by rule, so getRandomTarget runs again and draws again. (3) After every executed action, if the next queued item is a move, battle.ts recomputes getActionSpeed for every queued action. That is another draw each time while Milotic's Muddy Water or Struggle is still queued. (4) runMove calls getTarget once more, for another draw. Useful targets: Coil ('self') resolves to the user and never samples. Ice Beam and Hypnosis with a living chosen target never sample. If that chosen foe has fainted, every getTarget call samples. No draw happens when there are no living foes (randomFoe returns null).
mechanics.rng_draws: On turn 1, with Milotic moving 3rd after beforeTurn, Gholdengo's Protect and Grimmsnarl's Light Screen, a single Muddy Water consumed 6 random(2) draws in this order: resolveAction:269, resolveAction→getActionSpeed:275, runAction:2923 three times, then runMove:223.
mechanics.uncertainty: Probe-confirmed call sites and count. The count per turn depends on how many actions run before Milotic, i.e. on how many times battle.ts:2919 fires while the action is queued. Whether cartridge Champions consumes RNG this way is unknown; it is a Showdown artifact.

mechanics.name: Accuracy/crit/damage-roll/secondary draw order for Milotic's attacks
mechanics.behavior: Order within trySpreadMoveHit: Invulnerability, then TryHit (Protect, Good as Gold), then type immunity, then TryImmunity, then accuracy (one randomChance(acc,100) per remaining target unless acc === true), then the hit loop. The accuracy stage formula is acc*(3+b)/3 or acc*3/(3-b), truncated. Inside the hit loop, for each target: crit = randomChance(1,24) for critRatio 1 in gen 9, then basePower events, then base damage tr(tr(tr(22*BP*A)/D)/50). Then champions modifyDamage applies, in order: +2, spread 0.75 (modify), WeatherModifyDamage, crit ×1.5 (trunc), randomizer tr(tr(d*(100-random(16)))/100), STAB 1.5, type shifts (×2 per positive typeMod, trunc /2 per negative), burn (n/a, special), ModifyDamage (Light Screen 2732/4096 in doubles, skipped on crit), a minimum of 1, and finally 16-bit trunc. A crit ignores Milotic's negative SpA stages and the target's positive SpD stages. After spreadDamage and runMoveEffects come secondaries: one random(100) per secondary per non-false target. DamagingHit (Stamina) runs after secondaries. Update eachEvent speed-sorts active Pokemon, and equal speeds shuffle.
mechanics.champions_override: modifyDamage, spreadMoveHit and hitStepMoveHitLoop are replaced by champions scripts.ts. The arithmetic matches base; the differences are log args, AfterHit when the source fainted, and Emergency Exit checks.
mechanics.rng_draws: see behavior; all via prng.random (randomChance(n,d) = random(d) < n)
mechanics.uncertainty: Probe traces matched this order for Muddy Water, Ice Beam and Hypnosis. The residual phase also showed an extra prng.shuffle from fieldEvent speed ties between field handlers. That draw is not Milotic-specific but occurs in the same turns.

mechanics.name: Rain (Politoed Drizzle) / Sun (Charizard-Mega-Y Drought) effects on Milotic
mechanics.behavior: Drizzle and Drought set weather in onStart, i.e. on switch-in or Mega Evolution. Neither item needed for extended duration is held (Damp Rock / Heat Rock), so weather lasts 5 turns. Rain: Water moves ×1.5 via onWeatherModifyDamage (defender.effectiveWeather), so Milotic's Muddy Water is boosted. Sun: Water ×0.5, so Muddy Water is weakened, and sunnyday.onImmunity blocks new freezes from Ice Beam (probe-verified). Weather does not change Ice Beam, Coil or Hypnosis. Milotic takes no weather damage, since neither sand nor hail/snow is present. The multiplier is applied through priorityEvent('WeatherModifyDamage') after the spread modifier. No Utility Umbrella, Cloud Nine or Air Lock exists.
mechanics.uncertainty: Probe: Muddy Water into Mega Charizard Y in sun went from base 35 to 36 final (0.5 sun × 2 SE × 1.5 STAB), and frz in sun returned false.

mechanics.name: Grassy Terrain (ally Rillaboom Grassy Surge) on Milotic
mechanics.behavior: Grassy Terrain is set by ally Rillaboom's Grassy Surge and lasts 5 turns (no Terrain Extender). Milotic is grounded, so in the residual phase (onResidualOrder 5, subOrder 2) it heals trunc(baseMaxhp/16) = trunc(12.625) = 12 when below max HP. The terrain boosts Grass moves by grounded attackers ×5325/4096. That applies to foe Farigiraf's Grass Knot against Milotic, which is super effective. It gives Milotic's own moves no boost. It halves Earthquake, Bulldoze and Magnitude, none of which are in these sets.
mechanics.uncertainty: The heal amount is derived from code and was not probed.

mechanics.name: Milotic's weight vs Grass Knot (foe Farigiraf)
mechanics.behavior: Grass Knot's basePowerCallback uses target.getWeight(), which is weighthg after the ModifyWeight event with a floor of 1. No weight modifiers exist in these teams. Milotic has 1620 hg, which falls in the >=1000 band, so Grass Knot has BP 100 against it. Grass is super effective against Water (typechart water Grass:1). The move has the contact flag and is boosted in Grassy Terrain because Farigiraf is grounded. No Low Kick, Heavy Slam or Heat Crash exists in either team.

mechanics.name: Foe Light Screen / Reflect (Grimmsnarl, Light Clay) vs Milotic's attacks
mechanics.behavior: Light Screen is a side condition lasting 5 turns, or 8 with Light Clay, which Grimmsnarl holds. onAnyModifyDamage applies chainModify(2732/4096) to Special moves hitting its side in doubles, unless the hit is a crit or the move infiltrates. This reduces Milotic's Muddy Water, per target, and Ice Beam. Reflect is analogous for Physical moves, which here means only Struggle. The modifier runs in the ModifyDamage stage of modifyDamage, after STAB and type effectiveness. Status moves (Hypnosis, Coil) are unaffected.
mechanics.uncertainty: The Reflect data entry was not re-read here; it is assumed symmetric with Light Screen and should be verified in the Grimmsnarl slice.

mechanics.name: Protect blocking Milotic's moves
mechanics.behavior: Muddy Water, Ice Beam, Hypnosis and Struggle all have flags.protect, so the protect volatile's onTryHit blocks them with '-activate Protect' and returns NOT_FAIL. That happens in the TryHit step, before accuracy, so a protected target consumes no accuracy, crit, roll or secondary draws. For Muddy Water, the non-protected foe is still hit and still takes the 0.75 spread modifier. Coil has no protect flag and targets self. Champions sets Protect's base PP to 5, which calculatePP turns into 8 for the foes. The stall counter draws randomChance(1, counter) on consecutive Protects, but those draws belong to the protecting Pokemon.
mechanics.uncertainty: The spread-with-one-protected case was confirmed by probe.

mechanics.name: Team B abilities triggered by Milotic's hits (Stamina, Emergency Exit) and non-interactions
mechanics.behavior: Archaludon's Stamina raises Def +1 in onDamagingHit for each damaging hit from Milotic, including each Muddy Water hit. That Def is irrelevant to Milotic's special moves but it changes state. Golisopod's Emergency Exit (champions override) sets switchFlag when a hit takes it from above 1/2 max HP to at or below 1/2, provided canSwitch and no switch or force-switch flag is already set. Unlike base, the override does not clear other actives' switchFlags. The checks run in champions hitStepMoveHitLoop after afterMoveSecondaryEvent. Golisopod-Mega has Tough Claws instead. Non-interactions: Politoed's set ability is Drizzle, not Water Absorb, and no Storm Drain, Sap Sipper or Dry Skin is in either set, so Muddy Water is never absorbed or redirected. Farigiraf's Armor Tail only blocks priority > 0.1, and all of Milotic's moves are priority 0. Grimmsnarl's Prankster and Charizard's Blaze do not react to Milotic's moves. Neither team has Covert Cloak, Shield Dust or Sheer Force, so all secondaries apply.
mechanics.champions_override: emergencyexit.onEmergencyExit overridden (no clearing of other actives' switchFlag).
mechanics.uncertainty: Emergency Exit via Milotic's spread hit is inferred from code and was not probed.

mechanics.name: Ally-targeted Ice Beam / Hypnosis and ally abilities
mechanics.behavior: The 'normal' target class allows the adjacent ally in doubles: validTargetLoc for a negative loc requires |targetLoc - sourceLoc| === 1, so self is invalid. Ally abilities that change the outcome: Gholdengo's Good as Gold blocks Hypnosis, a Status move targeting it, with '-immune' and no accuracy draw (probe-verified). Raichu-Mega-Y's No Guard (onAnyAccuracy returns true when source or target is the holder) makes Milotic's Ice Beam or Hypnosis on it skip the accuracy draw. Lightning Rod (non-Mega Raichu) only redirects Electric moves, so it does not affect Milotic's moves. Flash Fire (Ceruledge) does not react to Ice or Water. mechanics.name: Stat-stage engine as exercised by Milotic
mechanics.behavior: Battle.boost returns 0 if the target has no HP, and false if it is inactive or no foes remain (gen>5). It runs ChangeBoost, then getCappedBoost (±6), then TryBoost. Then for each stat it applies boostBy. A nonzero change logs -boost or -unboost and fires AfterEachBoost, which is how Competitive hooks in. A zero change from a primary move logs '<msg> stat 0'; a zero change from a secondary or self effect is silent. AfterBoost fires at the end. Battle.boost returns success true or null. Accuracy and evasion stages feed the hitStepAccuracy formula. Atk/SpA/Def/SpD stages feed calculateStat, and crits ignore the harmful stages.

This is stored as pokemon.canMegaEvo when the Pokemon is constructed. canMegaEvoY is undefined outside Let's Go, so the command is the plain 'mega' suffix ('move N T mega'), not 'megay'.

Choice rules: the request exposes canMegaEvo only when the Pokemon is not locked. If Struggle is forced, lockedMove = 'struggle' and the mega option disappears. side.chooseMove rejects mega if pokemon.canMegaEvo is falsy or if side.choice.mega is already set this turn, so ally Staraptor (Staraptite) and Raichu cannot both mega in one turn. Once a mega resolves, canMegaEvo = false for every Pokemon on that side, so there is one Mega per side per battle, shared with Staraptor.

Timing: the mega action (order 104) is unshifted before Raichu's move action (order 200). It therefore runs after switches (103) and before every move, whatever the move's priority, and it happens even if the move is later stopped (flinch, sleep, or a Protect-blocked target).

Effects (champions formeChange with isPermanent=true and source=item): setSpecies runs. mechanics.name: Lightning Rod (base Raichu only)
mechanics.behavior:
Active while Raichu is in base forme (lost on Mega Evolution). It has two parts.

(1) onTryHit(target, source, move): if target !== source and move.type === 'Electric', it tries boost {spa:+1}. If the boost fails (already +6), it shows '-immune'. Either way it returns null, so the move does nothing to Raichu. This runs in hitStepTryHitEvent (step 1) and so precedes the type-immunity, accuracy and damage steps: no accuracy draw is consumed for Raichu as the target.

(2) onAnyRedirectTarget: for any Electric move without the pledgecombo flag, it maps a target class of randomNormal/adjacentFoe to 'normal' and checks validTarget(Raichu, user, class). In doubles every other slot is adjacent, so any single-target Electric move from another Pokemon is redirected to Raichu, with '-activate ... Lightning Rod' shown when it changes the target. Redirection is invoked only in Pokemon.getMoveTargets' default (single-target) branch, and only when activePerHalf > 1 and !move.tracksTarget. Spread moves are never redirected. Weather Ball resolves its type before getMoveTargets and is never Electric (Normal, Water in rain, Fire in sun). Team A has no Electric move other than Raichu's own.

Ordering with Protect: the Protect volatile's onTryHit has onTryHitPriority 3, while Lightning Rod's onTryHit has default priority 0. If Raichu Protects, Protect's NOT_FAIL ends the event first, so no SpA boost is granted. The ability is breakable (flags.breakable), but no Mold Breaker-type ability exists in either team.

mechanics.name: activeMoveActions counter (Fake Out gating)
mechanics.behavior: Pokemon.activeMoveActions is initialised to 0, reset to 0 in switchIn (lead, manual switch, or replacement after a faint), and incremented at the start of every runMove, before BeforeMove, PP deduction, targeting or any failure. The champions Fake Out onDisableMove reads it during endTurn, and it must be part of battle state. Raichu can enter only as a team-preview lead, by a player switch, or as a faint replacement. Team A has no pivot moves and no Emergency Exit or Eject effects, so every entry resets the counter to 0 and makes Fake Out available on the next move request.

mechanics.name: PP exhaustion / Struggle for Raichu
mechanics.behavior:
getMoves marks a slot disabled if pp <= 0 or moveSlot.disabled is set. If no slot is enabled, getMoveRequestData replaces the moves with [{Struggle, target 'randomNormal'}] and sets lockedMove = 'struggle', which also removes canMegaEvo from the request. side.chooseMove then pushes moveid 'struggle' with no target or mega. Raichu's slots are Zap Cannon 8, Focus Blast 8, Fake Out 12 and Protect 8 PP. Because the champions Fake Out disable makes Fake Out unselectable after the first action, Raichu is forced into Struggle once Zap Cannon, Focus Blast and Protect reach 0 PP, even with Fake Out PP left. The exception is a turn where activeMoveActions == 0 (fresh entry), when Fake Out is available.

Struggle: typeless (onModifyMove sets type '???', so it gets no STAB, has 1x effectiveness and hits Ghosts), Physical, 50 BP, accuracy true, priority 0, flags contact and protect. After damage, struggleRecoil deals directDamage of clampIntRange(round(baseMaxhp/4), 1) = 41 HP for Raichu, with an EmergencyExit check (none on Raichu). Target: when the action is resolved in the queue with no targetLoc, getRandomTarget samples from the adjacent foes. runMove -> getTarget samples again because randomNormal always goes through getRandomTarget. If no foe is alive it resolves to the opposite slot and the move fails with notarget. It is never redirected by Lightning Rod or No Guard effects (type '???'). Burn halves it; Reflect reduces it. PP is not deducted (runMove special-cases struggle).
mechanics.rng_draws: random(n) target sample at queue resolve (n = adjacent foes, a draw even when n == 1), a second random(n) sample in getTarget, random(24) crit, random(16) damage. No accuracy draw.
mechanics.uncertainty: The double random-target draw (at queue resolve and again in getTarget) is inferred from reading the code paths, not from a sim run; it should be pinned with a PS reference fixture.

mechanics.name: Single-target 'normal' targeting in doubles (Zap Cannon, Focus Blast, Fake Out)
mechanics.behavior:
targetTypeChoices('normal') is true, so in doubles a targetLoc is mandatory ('needs a target'). validTargetLoc('normal') accepts any adjacent slot: both foe slots (+1, +2) and the ally slot (negative loc). Self is never valid. Validity is positional, so a fainted or empty slot is still a legal choice. Protect (target 'self') must have no targetLoc.

Execution: getTarget returns the chosen Pokemon if it is unfainted. A fainted chosen foe is retargeted by getRandomTarget, which samples uniformly among the living adjacent foes (a draw). A fainted chosen ally is not retargeted, so the move fails with notarget. If both foes are fainted, the move resolves to the opposite slot and fails.

In getMoveTargets, RedirectTarget (Lightning Rod elsewhere; none on Team B) applies after the retarget. Choice domain per non-Struggle move request: 3 target choices each for Zap Cannon, Focus Blast and Fake Out (Fake Out only while enabled), plus Protect, and each of these doubled by 'mega' while canMegaEvo is set and side.choice.mega is not. Switch options to the non-fainted bench (at most 2 of the 4 picked) are added; no trapping exists in either team.
mechanics.uncertainty: PS accepts targeting a fainted or empty slot because the check is positional. DuoForge must decide explicitly whether that belongs in the model-facing command domain; excluding it silently would diverge from the reference.

mechanics.name: Damage formula as used by Raichu's attacks (champions modifyDamage)
mechanics.behavior:
getDamage computes the base damage: level 50, baseDamage = tr(tr(tr(tr(2*50/5+2)*BP*A)/D)/50). A and D come from calculateStat with boosts; a crit ignores the attacker's negative boosts and the defender's positive boosts. The Modify{Atk,SpA,Def,SpD} events then apply, but none are relevant to Raichu. The crit roll happens before the BasePower event. No BasePower modifiers apply to Raichu's moves in this matchup: Grassy Terrain boosts only Grass and weakens only EQ/Bulldoze/Magnitude, and Raichu holds no type-boosting item.

Champions modifyDamage then runs in this order: +2; spread x0.75 only if hitting more than one target (never for Raichu's single-target moves); WeatherModifyDamage (rain and sun affect only Water and Fire, so no effect); crit tr(x*1.5); random roll tr(tr(x*(100-random(16)))/100); STAB 1.5 via battle.modify for Electric moves (Zap Cannon only, both formes); type effectiveness by repeated doubling or tr-halving, clamped to -6..6; burn x0.5 via modify for Physical moves (Fake Out, Struggle) if Raichu is burned; ModifyDamage event (Reflect for Physical or Light Screen for Special, 2732/4096 in doubles, skipped on crit; Raichu has no Life Orb); zbroken x0.25 (unreachable); min 1; then 16-bit truncation. The STAB check also uses getTypes(false, true), which does not matter without Tera.

mechanics.name: Priority / dynamic speed ordering affecting Raichu
mechanics.behavior: Actions are sorted by comparePriority: order ascending (switch 103, mega 104, moves 200, residual 300), then priority descending, then speed descending, then subOrder and effectOrder. Ties are resolved by prng.shuffle inside speedSort. In gen >= 8, after every action whose next queue entry is a move, the battle calls updateSpeed, recomputes getActionSpeed for all queued actions and re-sorts. Mega Evolution speed, Tailwind, paralysis and Trick Room changes therefore apply mid-turn. The champions Pokemon.getActionSpeed override uses speed = getStat('spe') (capped at 10000), negated under Trick Room, with no 13-bit truncation. Raichu's brackets: Protect +4, Fake Out +3, everything else 0. Raichu's effective Spe: 178 base / 200 Mega; x2 under Team A Tailwind; x0.5 paralysed (unreachable for Raichu).
mechanics.champions_override: data/mods/champions/scripts.ts:46-54 replaces the base 10000-speed Trick Room formula with -speed

mechanics.name: Speed tie: base Raichu (178) vs Staraptor-Mega (178)
mechanics.behavior: With the given spreads the only exact speed tie involving Raichu is with ally Staraptor after it mega-evolves: Spe 110+32+20 = 162, Jolly x1.1 gives 178. That equals base Raichu's 162 x1.1 = 178. The two are mutually compatible because only one Team A Mega is allowed, and it is Staraptor's. Tailwind (x2 to both, 356) and Trick Room (-178 each) preserve the tie. Every speedSort containing both actions in the same order and priority bracket shuffles them: the initial queue sort, each gen-9 dynamic re-sort, eachEvent/Update, and residual handler ordering such as the Grassy Terrain heal. Each shuffle consumes a draw. Other speeds (Charizard/Mega-Y 163, Staraptor 167, Gholdengo 118, Archaludon 114, Rillaboom 113) do not tie with Raichu (178) or Raichu-Mega-Y (200).

mechanics.name: Accuracy roll for Raichu's moves
mechanics.behavior: In hitStepAccuracy, per target: accuracy = ModifyAccuracy event (no modifiers in either team). If the accuracy is not true, it is adjusted by the accuracy/evasion stage difference, clamped to ±6, as tr(acc*(3+b)/3) or tr(acc*3/(3-b)). Then the Accuracy event runs (No Guard can return true), and a Pokemon using a self-target status move sets it to true. If accuracy !== true, randomChance(acc, 100) is drawn, which also happens for 100-accuracy Fake Out. Moves in scope: Zap Cannon 50, Focus Blast 70, Fake Out 100 each draw; Protect and Struggle never draw. The draw is skipped for targets already removed by an earlier step: Protect (TryHit), Lightning Rod absorption, type immunity or Armor Tail (TryMove).

A crit multiplies by 1.5 in modifyDamage, ignores the attacker's negative offensive boosts and the defender's positive defensive boosts, and bypasses Reflect/Light Screen. No CriticalHit blockers (Battle Armor, Shell Armor, Lucky Chant) exist.

mechanics.name: Good as Gold
mechanics.behavior: onTryHit(target, source, move): if move.category === 'Status' && target !== source, it adds '-immune' [from] ability: Good as Gold and returns null. This runs in hit step 1 (TryHit) of trySpreadMoveHit, which is the path for all Pokémon-targeting moves. A null result becomes false and removes the target; no '-fail' is printed because the result is null, not false. The move then does nothing to Gholdengo. It does NOT fire for: (a) self-targeted status moves (Nasty Plot, Protect), because target === source; (b) field and side moves (Trick Room 'all'; Reflect, Light Screen, Tailwind 'allySide'), which go through tryMoveHit and TryHitField/TryHitSide rather than TryHit; (c) damaging moves with stat-drop secondaries (Snarl, Spirit Break, Psychic, Muddy Water); (d) abilities such as Intimidate. Flag breakable: Mold Breaker, Teravolt or Turboblaze would ignore it, but none of the 16 abilities reachable across both teams do. Reachable blocks here: (1) Grimmsnarl's Prankster Parting Shot on Gholdengo fails entirely: no Atk/SpA drop, and Grimmsnarl does NOT switch, because selfSwitch is only set in runMoveEffects, which is never reached once every target has failed at TryHit. (2) Ally Milotic's Hypnosis, if targeted at Gholdengo, is blocked. Hypnosis is the only sleep source in the closure, so sleep is unreachable for Gholdengo. The Prankster Dark-immunity check (step 3) is never reached, and Gholdengo is not Dark anyway.
interactions: Parting Shot (Grimmsnarl, Prankster) blocked, no user switch
Hypnosis from ally Milotic blocked, so sleep is unreachable
Protect volatile (onTryHitPriority 3) runs before Good as Gold on the same TryHit; only the message differs
Does not stop Snarl/Spirit Break SpA drops (damaging moves)
mechanics.rng_draws: none; blocking happens before the accuracy step, so a blocked Parting Shot/Hypnosis consumes no accuracy draw against Gholdengo

mechanics.name: Life Orb
mechanics.behavior: onModifyDamage: chainModify([5324, 4096]) in the final ModifyDamage step (after STAB, type effectiveness and burn; before the min-1 check and 16-bit truncation). For spread moves it applies once per target. onAfterMoveSecondarySelf: if source !== target && move.category !== 'Status' && !source.forceSwitchFlag, it deals this.damage(baseMaxhp/10) = trunc(17.9) = 17 HP to Gholdengo (Pokemon.damage truncates). AfterMoveSecondarySelf fires once per move from useMoveInner, and only when moveResult is true (at least one target survived all hit steps) and the user lacks Sheer Force. So there is no recoil for Shadow Ball into Farigiraf (Normal-type immunity), into Protect, or on a miss; none for a double-missed or double-protected Make It Rain; recoil happens once for a Make It Rain that hits two targets, and also when the move KOs targets. Status moves (Nasty Plot, Protect) get neither the boost nor recoil. Struggle (Physical) gets both the boost and the 17 HP recoil, on top of its own recoil. Combined with Grimmsnarl's Light Screen, chainModify gives ((4096*5324+2048)>>12 = 5324), then ((5324*2732+2048)>>12) = 3551/4096 in either order. Magic Guard, Klutz, Magic Room, Embargo, Knock Off, Trick and Thief are absent from both teams, so the item is always active and cannot be removed. The recoil goes through spreadDamage/Damage events; no modifiers exist in this matchup.
interactions: LO recoil can KO Gholdengo after it KOs the last foe: see implicit-faint-and-win-order
LO applies to Struggle (boost and 17 HP recoil in addition to 45 Struggle recoil)
EmergencyExit event runs on Gholdengo when recoil crosses 50% HP (no effect; Gholdengo lacks the ability)
mechanics.rng_draws: none

mechanics.name: Make It Rain
mechanics.behavior: Base: num 874, BP 120, Special, Steel, pp 5 (champions max PP 8), priority 0, flags {protect, mirror}, target allAdjacentFoes, no secondaries, no handlers. Champions override: accuracy 95 (base 100) and self boosts {spa: -2} (base -1). The player chooses no target; chooseMove rejects a target location. Targets are all active non-fainted foes, in foe slot order. spreadHit = true if more than one target at the start of trySpreadMoveHit, even if one is later removed by Protect or a miss; each hit target then takes 0.75x via modify. With only one foe active there is no spread reduction. Per target, in order: TryHit (Protect removes the target), type immunity (no foe is immune to Steel), accuracy 95 (reduced by Gholdengo's accuracy stage, e.g. from Muddy Water), then damage. STAB 1.5, Life Orb 1.3 per target, Light Screen 2732/4096 on non-crits. After damage, selfDrops runs once per move (move.selfDropped): it draws random(100) even though self has no chance field, then applies spa -2 to Gholdengo. This happens only if at least one target is still in the target list after effects, and battle.boost returns false (no drop) when the foe side has 0 Pokémon left, so a game-winning Make It Rain does not lower SpA. The drop is capped at -6. Effectiveness vs Team B: Politoed 0.5, Golisopod (Bug/Water) 0.5, Mega Golisopod (Bug/Steel) 0.5, Archaludon (Steel/Dragon) 0.5, Farigiraf (Normal/Psychic) 1, Charizard/Charizard-Mega-Y (Fire/Flying) 0.5, Grimmsnarl (Dark/Fairy) 2. Life Orb recoil and the Emergency Exit checks follow.

mechanics.name: Drizzle
mechanics.behavior:
onStart calls this.field.setWeather('raindance'). There is a guard for Kyogre holding Blue Orb, which is unreachable. flags {}. The champions mod has no override.

When it fires: in gen>=5 an ability's onStart runs as the SwitchIn handler (getCallback). So it fires on every switch-in: the lead switch-in at battle start ('start' action), end-of-turn replacement after a faint, and mid-turn entry after ally Grimmsnarl's Parting Shot (selfSwitch) or ally Golisopod's Emergency Exit. Simultaneous switch-ins are batched in runSwitch and ordered by speedSort, using a fractional speedOrder offset for SwitchIn.

setWeather semantics:
- If the weather is already 'raindance' and the source effect is an Ability (gen>5), it returns false silently. There is no message and the duration is not refreshed.
- Otherwise the SetWeather event runs (no handlers in these teams), the current weather is replaced (e.g. Mega Charizard Y's sun), and weatherState.duration is set by durationCallback: 5 (8 only with Damp Rock, which is absent).
- The FieldStart message is '-weather RainDance [from] ability: Drizzle [of] Politoed'. The gen<=5 permanent-weather branch does not apply.

Drizzle has no onEnd, so rain persists after Politoed switches out or faints. No ability-changing or suppressing effects exist in the 12 sets (no Skill Swap, Neutralizing Gas, Cloud Nine or Air Lock).

- Accuracy: 85, scaled by the attacker's accuracy stage minus the target's evasion stage (trunc(acc*(3+b)/3) or trunc(acc*3/(3-b))).
- Damage.
- Secondary roll.

The secondary boost goes through battle.boost, which returns 0 for a 0-HP target; the roll is still drawn. Contrary (Staraptor-Mega) inverts the drop to +1 accuracy. Competitive (Milotic) triggers +2 SpA via AfterEachBoost because the source is a foe. At -6 nothing happens.

mechanics.behavior:
Data: Status, priority +4, accuracy true, target 'self' (no target choice), flags {noassist, failcopycat} (their callers are unreachable), stallingMove. Champions PP override 5, so max 8.

onPrepareHit returns !!queue.willAct() && runEvent('StallMove'). It fails with no RNG draw if no move, switch, instaswitch or shift action remains in the queue, i.e. Politoed acts last this turn. For example, all four actives choose Protect and Politoed is slowest.

The StallMove event only has a handler while the 'stall' volatile exists (volatile-stall). The accuracy check is bypassed (self-target Status). On success:
- the 'protect' volatile is added (duration 1, removed at this turn's residual), with message '-singleturn Protect';
- onHit calls addVolatile('stall').

The protect volatile's onTryHit (priority 3) returns NOT_FAIL and prints '-activate Protect' for every move with flags.protect, unless the HitProtect event says otherwise (Unseen Fist; absent here). Every foe-targeting move in both teams has flags.protect, including Fake Out, Hypnosis, spread moves and Parting Shot. On a spread move only this target is removed; the spread modifier still applies to the other target. The lockedmove reset branch is unreachable.

Volatile durations are decremented in the Residual fieldEvent. So if Politoed does not successfully Protect on the next turn, stall expires at that turn's residual and the next Protect has a 100% chance with no draw. A switch-out clears all volatiles (champions clearVolatile).

When no move is selectable, getMoveRequestData offers only Struggle and side.chooseMove pushes moveid 'struggle' with no target. The only disabling source reachable here is 0 PP: there is no Disable, Encore, Taunt, Torment, Imprison, Choice item or Assault Vest.

- onModifyMove sets type '???': no STAB, no type effectiveness, so it hits Ghosts (Ceruledge, Gholdengo).

mechanics.name: Politoed player-selectable command domain (doubles)

Team preview: Picked Team Size=Auto means 4 of 6 in doubles; Politoed may be picked and ordered. Open Team Sheets reveals the full set.

Per-turn choices while active:
- 'move 1 T' Weather Ball and 'move 3 T' Ice Beam need a target in doubles. Valid T: the two foe locs (+1, +2) and the adjacent-ally loc. Self loc is invalid. validTargetLoc checks geometry only, so an empty or fainted slot is accepted and resolved at execution.

- Moves at 0 PP are disabled; if all are disabled, only Struggle is sent.

- No mega, tera, zmove or dynamax flag is ever legal.

Maximum: 8 move commands (3+1+3+1) plus switches.

mechanics.behavior:
getTarget:
- Chosen loc holds an unfainted Pokemon: use it.
- Chosen foe has fainted, or the slot is empty: getRandomTarget, which in doubles returns side.randomFoe() (sample over alive foes) or foe.active[0].
- Chosen ally has fainted: no retarget. getMoveTargets then returns [] and useMoveInner fails with [notarget].
- No alive foe: randomFoe returns null with no draw; foe.active[0] (fainted) is used and the move fails.

RedirectTarget runs but has no effect: Lightning Rod redirects only Electric moves, and there is no Storm Drain or Follow Me.

mechanics.name: Spread-hit pipeline used by Muddy Water
mechanics.behavior:
trySpreadMoveHit sets spreadHit if more than one target, then runs Try/PrepareHit and these steps, filtering targets after each:
0. Invulnerability.
1. TryHit (Protect, Flash Fire, Good as Gold, Lightning Rod).
2. Type immunity.
3. TryImmunity (powder, prankster).
4. Accuracy.
5. Break protect.
6. Steal boosts.
7. Hit loop.

The hit loop (champions hitStepMoveHitLoop) calls champions spreadMoveHit. The substitute check comes first (no Substitute here). Then getSpreadDamage, spreadDamage, and runMoveEffects. Then selfDrops and secondaries. Then DamagingHit (Stamina, freeze-thaw-by-Fire), then EmergencyExit checks. After the loop: gotAttacked, AfterMoveSecondary events, and a target EmergencyExit when crossing half HP.

mechanics.name: Damage calculation path for Politoed's attacks
mechanics.behavior:
getDamage:
1. Immunity.
2. basePower after ModifyMove (Weather Ball 100 in weather).
3. Crit: critRatio defaults to 1 (the Dex move default), so randomChance(1,24). No crit-ratio modifiers exist in these sets.
4. BasePower event (Mystic Water 4915/4096).
5. SpA/SpD with boosts: a crit ignores the attacker's negative and the defender's positive stages. ModifySpA/ModifySpD events (Flash Fire only for Ceruledge's own moves).
6. base = floor(floor(floor(22*BP*A)/D)/50).

Champions modifyDamage:
1. +2.
2. Spread 0.75.
3. WeatherModifyDamage.
4. Crit trunc(x1.5).
5. Random: trunc(x*(100-random(16))/100).
6. STAB 1.5 via ModifySTAB (no tera).
7. Type effectiveness, doubling/halving with trunc per step, clamped to +/-6.
8. Burn halving (physical only; Struggle).
9. ModifyDamage: Light Screen 2732/4096 in doubles when Politoed hits a Team B ally under Grimmsnarl's screen; no Life Orb on Politoed.
10. bypassProtect x0.25 (unreachable).
11. If 0, then 1.
12. 16-bit trunc.

battle.modify = trunc((trunc(v*trunc(num*4096/den)) + 2047)/4096).
mechanics.champions_override: The champions modifyDamage (scripts.ts:196-312) differs from base only in the protocol arguments for 4x/0.25x effectiveness messages (scripts.ts:270,277). The arithmetic is identical.
interactions: Light Screen on Politoed's own side when hitting an ally
mechanics.uncertainty: The arithmetic was diffed statically between base and champions. Damage values were not computed or verified at runtime.

mechanics.name: Drizzle vs Mega Charizard Y's Drought (same team)
mechanics.behavior:
Charizard-Mega-Y has ability Drought. On mega evolution, champions formeChange runs setAbility(..., isFromFormeChange=true), and setAbility runs the ability Start. So Drought sets sun during the megaEvo action, overwriting rain. Rain to sun is a different weather, so it is not blocked.

Politoed switching in later replaces sun with rain again.

On simultaneous switch-ins (e.g. both replacing fainted allies at end of turn, with Charizard already Mega), handlers run in speed order. Charizard (163) runs Drought first, then Politoed (94) Drizzle, so rain wins. Under Trick Room the champions getActionSpeed returns -speed, so Politoed resolves first and sun wins.

In sun, Politoed's kit changes:
- Weather Ball becomes Fire 100 (absorbed by Flash Fire; thaws on hit).
- Muddy Water is halved.
- Ice Beam cannot freeze.

interactions: Hurricane accuracy is 50 in sun and true in rain (data/moves.ts:9035-9045)

mechanics.name: Politoed switch-in/out and faint lifecycle
mechanics.behavior:
switchIn: the old active gets BeforeSwitchOut/SwitchOut, its ability and item End events, and clearVolatile. The champions clearVolatile resets boosts (e.g. the -1 Atk from Intimidate and accuracy drops from Muddy Water), removes volatiles (protect, stall) and clears lastMove.

The new active is placed, then runSwitch. Drizzle fires in the SwitchIn fieldEvent. Status (frz/par/slp) and its counters persist.

On faint: rain persists because Drizzle has no End. The side needs a replacement at end of turn if its bench is non-empty; fainted Politoed's slot then takes the replacement, and Drizzle does not re-trigger. Mid-turn entry via ally Parting Shot (selfSwitch) or Emergency Exit (champions override) triggers Drizzle immediately.

HP is shown to the opponent as a Champions floor percentage.

hitStepAccuracy runs once per target after TryHit and type immunity. Steps:
1. ModifyAccuracy.
2. Stage adjustment (the attacker's accuracy stage minus the target's evasion stage, clamped to +/-6; trunc(acc*(3+b)/3) or trunc(acc*3/(3-b))).
3. Accuracy event: No Guard returns true.

Then randomChance(accuracy,100) is drawn even when accuracy is 100 or more (e.g. 133). No draw when accuracy===true: Protect (self-target Status), Struggle, or No Guard involvement.

mechanics.name: Champions stat-point stat formula (Lv50)
mechanics.behavior: This format has no Level Clause Mod, so champions statModify takes the non-level branch. HP = base + SP + 75. Other stats = base + SP + 20. The nature is then applied as tr(tr(stat*110,16)/100) for plus and tr(tr(stat*90,16)/100) for minus. tr = unsigned trunc (num>>>0, or mod 2^bits). IVs play no part in the formula, but the validator requires every IV to be 31. SP is capped at 32 per stat and 66 in total (evLimit 66 for champions mods). Stats are recalculated through spreadModify inside setSpecies on every species change, including Mega. Max HP goes through updateMaxHp, which does nothing when the HP stat is unchanged. The level is forced to 50 by Adjust Level = 50. Level 50 enters the damage formula but not this stat formula.
mechanics.champions_override: Replaces base statModify (sim/battle.ts:2354-2372).

mechanics.name: Champions PP formula
mechanics.behavior: At dex init, champions caps any base move PP above 20 down to 20. calculatePP returns move.pp when noPPBoosts, otherwise (pp/5+1)*4. The ppUps argument is ignored. Golisopod's max PP: Leech Life 10 -> 12. Iron Head 15 -> 16. Drill Run 10 -> 12. Protect has champions base PP 5 -> 8. That is 48 move uses in total before PP exhaustion forces Struggle. No PP drain (Pressure, Spite) exists on either team.

mechanics.name: Golisopod-Mega forme and forme-change effects
mechanics.behavior: Golisopod-Mega: Bug/Steel. Base stats 75/150/175/70/120/40. Ability Tough Claws. Weight 148 kg (1480 hg). requiredItem Golisopite. isMega and battleOnly are derived from forme 'Mega'. Stats I computed: HP 182, Atk 222, Def 195, SpA 81, SpD 141, Spe 61. Mega happens through runMegaEvo -> champions formeChange(speciesId, item, isPermanent=true). Steps: (1) setSpecies replaces the types (Bug/Water -> Bug/Steel), recalculates stats, and updates weighthg. Stat boosts are kept (for example an Intimidate -1). (2) baseSpecies is set to Golisopod-Mega, a detailschange line is logged, and updateMaxHp runs. HP is unchanged (base HP 75 in both formes), so current HP is unchanged. (3) A '-mega' log line is added and moveThisTurnResult is set to true. (4) setAbility(Tough Claws, isFromFormeChange=true) runs. Emergency Exit's End runs (it has no handler) and baseAbility becomes toughclaws, so the ability survives switching. (5) On switch-out, champions clearVolatile calls setSpecies(baseSpecies). Because baseSpecies is now the Mega, the Mega persists. (6) Champions formeChange never sets formeRegression for item megas, so the Mega does not revert on faint. Consequences: Iron Head gains STAB. Emergency Exit is gone for the rest of the battle. The defensive type chart changes. Speed is unchanged at 61. Grass Knot BP is unchanged at 100.

mechanics.name: Mega Evolution choice, ordering and one-per-side limit
mechanics.behavior: canMegaEvo is computed when the Pokemon is constructed. Champions canMegaEvo returns item.megaStone[baseSpecies.name], which is 'Golisopod-Mega'. The Mega-Rayquaza branch does not apply (no requiredMove). Choice rules: 'move N [target] mega' is legal only if pokemon.canMegaEvo is set, and only one mega per side per turn (side.choice.mega). runMegaEvo sets canMegaEvo = false on every Pokemon of the side, so a side gets one Mega per battle. Team B also carries Charizard @ Charizardite Y, so at most one of Golisopod and Charizard can Mega Evolve per battle. Mega cannot be chosen while Golisopod must Struggle: the request strips canMegaEvo when all moves are disabled, and the Struggle action is pushed with no mega flag. Resolution: a move choice with mega adds a 'megaEvo' action with order 104. That is after switches (103) and before every move (order 200) whatever the move's priority, so the Mega is complete before Fake Out or Protect resolve that turn. The step is skipped if the user is Sky Dropped (not reachable here). megaEvo actions are ordered by getActionSpeed (negated under Trick Room), with ties shuffled. Because this is gen 9 (>= 8), whenever the next queued action is a move, runAction calls updateSpeed(), recomputes getActionSpeed for every queued action and re-sorts the queue. That covers the actions after a Mega. No Tera, Z or Dynamax exists in champions (canTerastallize returns null).
mechanics.champions_override: Champions canMegaEvo differs from base: there is no gen>=9 check on the target species and it keys megaStone by species.name. canTerastallize returns null.
mechanics.rng_draws: No direct draw. The queue re-sort after the megaEvo action can shuffle speed ties through prng.shuffle, and can draw for random targets through getActionSpeed -> getTarget.

mechanics.name: Emergency Exit
mechanics.behavior: Champions onEmergencyExit(target) returns early if battle.canSwitch(side) == 0 (no unfainted Pokemon in bench slots, index >= active.length), or if target.forceSwitchFlag or target.switchFlag is already set. Otherwise it sets target.switchFlag = true and logs '-activate ... ability: Emergency Exit'. Unlike base, it does not clear switchFlag on other active Pokemon. The EmergencyExit event fires when HP crosses from > maxhp/2 to <= maxhp/2 (182 max HP, trigger at <= 91 from > 91). Paths: (a) Target of a damaging move: after all hits, the Update event and the AfterMoveSecondary events, in hitStepMoveHitLoop. It uses HP-before = hurtThisTurn + damage (move.totalDamage for single-target moves, per-target damage for spread moves). It runs only if the target is still alive and the attacker lacks Sheer Force. REACHABLE through any damaging hit from Team A, or from an ally targeting Golisopod. (b) Attacker in spreadMoveHit after DamagingHit/AfterHit (contact recoil such as Rough Skin or Rocky Helmet): no such effect on either team, so UNREACHABLE. (c) Attacker after MoveFail (crash damage) or AfterMoveSecondarySelf (Life Orb): UNREACHABLE for this set. (d) Recoil in applyRecoilDamage: REACHABLE only through Struggle recoil. (e) End of the residual phase: Golisopod has no residual damage source in this matchup (only a Grassy Terrain heal), so UNREACHABLE. (f) After runSwitch (hazards): no hazards on either team, so UNREACHABLE. Each fresh crossing can trigger it again, for example after Leech Life drain or a Grassy Terrain heal lifts HP back above 91. The ability is lost permanently after Mega Evolution, and a turn's Mega happens before any damage that turn. Confusion self-hit damage has no EmergencyExit check in PS.
mechanics.champions_override: data/mods/champions/abilities.ts:22-29 removes base behaviour that set switchFlag = false on all actives of both sides (data/abilities.ts:1253-1257). With these two teams I found no observable difference: Team A has no pivot moves, and Parting Shot's own switch request is issued at the end of Grimmsnarl's action.
mechanics.uncertainty: Whether the Pokemon Champions cartridge matches PS on Emergency Exit timing (for example after drain or Update) is not verifiable from source. This mapping follows PS. The claim that the champions override is unobservable for these teams is my reasoning, not a test result.

mechanics.name: Mid-turn forced switch after Emergency Exit
mechanics.behavior: At the end of each runAction, any side with an active switchFlag is checked. If canSwitch == 0 the flags are cleared. Otherwise BeforeSwitchOut runs once per flagged Pokemon (no relevant handlers on Team B), then makeRequest('switch') runs and the turn loop pauses. getRequests('switch') gives a forceSwitch request only to sides with a flagged active. The other side gets no request (it waits). The chosen replacement becomes an 'instaswitch' action (order 3) because requestState == 'switch'. It is decremented from forcedSwitchesLeft and runs next through switchIn. If Golisopod's own move was still queued, it is skipped because Golisopod is no longer active. The replacement does not act this turn. The rest of the turn's queue continues afterwards. This is a single-player decision point inside the turn, which DuoForge's choice and secrecy model must represent.
mechanics.uncertainty: I did not trace switchIn internals, such as the exact point where abilities start on the replacement, for this entry.

mechanics.name: Tough Claws (Mega Golisopod)
mechanics.behavior: onBasePower (priority 21): if move.flags.contact, chainModify([5325,4096]). It applies in the BasePower event after the crit roll. runEvent then applies the chained modifier with battle.modify(), which rounds half down. All three of Golisopod's attacks (Leech Life, Iron Head, Drill Run) and Struggle are contact. Computed BP: 80 -> tr((80*5325+2047)/4096) = 104. Struggle 50 -> 65. The only other BasePower handler in this matchup is Grassy Terrain (priority 6), which never touches Golisopod's moves. Active only after Mega Evolution. No contact-punishing effects exist on either team: no Rough Skin, Iron Barbs, Rocky Helmet or Flame Body, and Raichu runs Lightning Rod, not Static. Contact therefore has no other consequence here.

mechanics.name: Leech Life
mechanics.behavior: Bug, Physical. BP 80. Accuracy 100. PP 10 (12 max in Champions). Priority 0. target 'normal' (any adjacent Pokemon, foe or ally, chosen). Flags: contact, protect, mirror, heal, metronome. drain [1,2]. No champions override. STAB (x1.5) in both formes. Tough Claws makes it 104 BP when Mega. The drain heals round(actual damage dealt / 2) to Golisopod (see implicit-drain-heal). Type effectiveness against Team A: Rillaboom 2x, Staraptor 0.5x, Mega Staraptor (Fighting/Flying) 0.25x, Milotic 1x, Ceruledge (Fire/Ghost) 0.25x, Raichu and Mega Raichu Y 1x, Gholdengo 0.25x. Against allies: Farigiraf 2x, Grimmsnarl 1x, Politoed 1x, Archaludon 0.5x, Charizard 0.25x. Blocked by Protect. No Heal Block, Liquid Ooze or Big Root exists in the matchup.

mechanics.name: Drain healing (Leech Life)
mechanics.behavior: Inside spreadDamage, right after the target's HP is reduced (gen > 4): amount = Math.round(targetDamage * 1/2). targetDamage is the actual damage dealt, capped by the target's remaining HP. battle.heal is then called with effect 'drain'. heal() forces an amount <= 1 up to 1, truncates, runs TryHeal (no handlers here), and fails silently if the healer has fainted, is inactive or is at full HP. Healing happens before the target's secondary effects, the Update event and the Emergency Exit check. Raising HP above 91 re-arms Golisopod's Emergency Exit.

mechanics.behavior: Steel, Physical. BP 80. Accuracy 100. PP 15 (16 max). Priority 0. target 'normal'. Flags: contact, protect, mirror, metronome. Secondary: 20% flinch in Champions (base 30%). STAB only once Mega (Bug/Steel). Tough Claws makes it 104 BP. The flinch matters only if the target has not yet acted this turn. Golisopod (Spe 61) is the slowest of all 12 sets, so this mainly applies under ally Farigiraf's Trick Room, or against a slowed or paralysed target. mechanics.name: Flinch
mechanics.behavior: Flinch volatile, duration 1. onBeforeMove (priority 8) logs 'cant', runs the Flinch event and returns false. BeforeMove runs before PP deduction, so a flinched move costs no PP. The volatile ends at the end of the turn, so a flinch landed after the target has already moved does nothing. Golisopod can inflict it with Iron Head (20%). Golisopod can receive it from Team A's Fake Out (100%, priority +3), which is blocked by Protect and by ally Farigiraf's Armor Tail, or from an ally's Iron Head aimed at it. A Mega chosen for the same turn still completes, because megaEvo (order 104) runs before moves.

mechanics.name: Drill Run
mechanics.behavior: Ground, Physical. BP 80. Accuracy 95. PP 10 (12 max). Priority 0. target 'normal'. Flags: contact, protect, mirror, metronome. critRatio 2, which is a 1/8 crit chance on the gen 7+ table. No STAB in either forme. Tough Claws makes it 104 BP. Type immunity (hit step 2, before accuracy; Ground uses isGrounded) makes it fail with '-immune' and no accuracy, crit or damage draws against Flying targets: Staraptor, Mega Staraptor, and ally Charizard / Mega Charizard Y. Effectiveness: Ceruledge 2x, Raichu and Mega Raichu Y 2x, Gholdengo 2x, Milotic 1x, Rillaboom 0.5x. Against allies: Archaludon 2x, Politoed 1x, Farigiraf 1x, Grimmsnarl 1x. Grassy Terrain does not halve it (the list is only Earthquake, Bulldoze and Magnitude). Accuracy after a Muddy Water -1 accuracy drop: trunc(95*3/4) = 71. Against Mega Raichu Y (No Guard) the accuracy is true and no draw happens.

mechanics.name: Protect
mechanics.behavior: Normal, Status. Priority +4. target 'self'. PP 5 in Champions (8 max). Flags: noassist, failcopycat. stallingMove. volatileStatus 'protect'. onPrepareHit returns !!queue.willAct() && runEvent('StallMove'): it fails if no move, switch, instaswitch or shift action remains in the queue (Golisopod acting last), or if the stall roll fails. onHit adds the 'stall' volatile. The protect volatile (duration 1, onTryHit priority 3) blocks any move with flags.protect unless checkMoveBypassesProtect says otherwise. It returns NOT_FAIL and logs '-activate'. For spread moves the block is per target. Every Team A move that could hit Golisopod has the protect flag, including Fake Out, Hypnosis, Muddy Water and Make It Rain. Neither team has a bypass (no Feint, Unseen Fist, Z or Max moves). Accuracy is true for a self-target Status move, so no accuracy draw. It can be combined with Mega in the same turn. PP is deducted even when the move fails.
mechanics.champions_override: PP 10 -> 5 (8 max after calculatePP).
mechanics.rng_draws: None on the first use. Consecutive uses draw through volatile-stall.

mechanics.name: Stall counter (consecutive Protect)
mechanics.behavior: The stall volatile has duration 2 and counterMax 729. On first add, counter = 3. onStallMove: success = randomChance(1, counter). On failure the stall volatile is deleted. On a successful re-add (onRestart), counter *= 3 while below 729, and the duration resets to 2. Consecutive success chance is therefore 1, 1/3, 1/9, 1/27 and so on. A turn without Protect lets it expire. Only Protect uses it on this set.
mechanics.rng_draws: random(counter) for each consecutive Protect (3, 9, 27, ... 729).

mechanics.name: PP deduction and exhaustion
mechanics.behavior: PP is deducted in runMove after BeforeMove passes (flinch, sleep, freeze, paralysis and confusion checks come first) and before useMove. deductPP subtracts 1 (no Pressure in the matchup) and clamps at 0. The move still runs even if it fails. A slot with pp <= 0 is marked disabled in the request. When no enabled move remains, the request offers only Struggle (target randomNormal). chooseMove then pushes {moveid:'struggle'} with no target and no mega. Golisopod has 48 total uses (12/16/12/8). Flat Rules has no turn limit or Endless Battle Clause, so exhaustion is reachable in principle.

mechanics.name: Struggle (implicit)
mechanics.behavior: Physical. BP 50. Accuracy true (no accuracy draw). noPPBoosts. Flags include contact and protect. onModifyMove sets the type to '???': no STAB, runImmunity returns true, and effectiveness is neutral against every target. target 'randomNormal', so a random live foe is chosen every time. struggleRecoil: after the hit loop, applyRecoilDamage deals clamp(round(baseMaxhp/4), 1) = round(45.5) = 46 HP to Golisopod through directDamage ('strugglerecoil' bypasses the Damage event). That recoil can trigger Emergency Exit if HP crosses 91. When Mega, Tough Claws applies (contact), giving 65 BP. Protect blocks it.
mechanics.rng_draws: Random-foe sample draws: in resolveAction (no targetLoc), in runMove -> getTarget, and in every getActionSpeed -> getTarget during a queue re-sort. Each draw consumes a PRNG call even with only one live foe. Plus crit random(24) and damage random(16).
mechanics.uncertainty: I have not verified the exact number of target-sample draws per turn for a queued Struggle. It depends on how many times the queue is re-sorted while the action is pending (sim/battle.ts:2919-2926).

mechanics.name: Damage calculation as applied to Golisopod's attacks
mechanics.behavior: getDamage steps: runImmunity. The basePower callback does not apply to Golisopod's moves. Crit roll (critRatio from ModifyCritRatio, no handlers here; table [0,24,8,2,1]). BasePower event (Tough Claws). A crit ignores Golisopod's negative Atk boosts and the target's positive Def boosts. calculateStat: stage multipliers 1, 1.5, 2 ... with floor. ModifyAtk/ModifyDef events: none for Golisopod; target-side Grassy Seed +1 Def on Ceruledge is a boost, not a modifier. base = tr(tr(tr(tr(2*50/5+2)*BP*Atk)/Def)/50). Champions modifyDamage then applies, in order: +2. Spread x0.75 (never for Golisopod's own single-target moves). WeatherModifyDamage (rain and sun do not affect Bug, Steel or Ground). Crit tr(x*1.5). Random tr(tr(x*(100-random(16)))/100). STAB modify 1.5. Type effectiveness: repeated x2, or tr(x/2). Burn halving: unreachable, because no move that can hit Golisopod inflicts burn (Heat Wave targets allAdjacentFoes only). ModifyDamage: Reflect when Golisopod hits its own ally under Grimmsnarl's Reflect, x2732/4096, not on a crit. Minimum 1. Final tr(x,16). Target-side consequences: Milotic's Sitrus Berry at <= 50% (Update event), and Archaludon's Stamina if an ally is hit.

mechanics.name: Golisopod type chart, both formes
mechanics.behavior: Defensive, Bug/Water: 2x from Flying, Rock, Electric. 0.5x from Fighting, Ground, Water, Ice, Steel. Fire and Grass are neutral (the two types cancel). Defensive, Mega Bug/Steel: Fire 4x. Grass 0.25x. 0.5x from Normal, Ice, Psychic, Bug, Dragon, Steel, Fairy. Poison immune, including psn/tox status and sandstorm, though none occurs here. Fighting, Ground, Flying, Rock, Electric and Water become neutral. Unchanged: Ice Beam 0.5x, Make It Rain 0.5x, Shadow Ball and Shadow Sneak 1x. Offensive multipliers are listed per move entry. mechanics.name: Target selection and retargeting for 'normal' moves
mechanics.behavior: Leech Life, Iron Head and Drill Run are 'normal': the player must supply a targetLoc in doubles. It may be either adjacent foe or the adjacent ally, never self (validTargetLoc and getTarget). Protect takes no target. At execution getTarget works like this. An unfainted Pokemon in the chosen slot is the target. A fainted ally is kept as the target and the move fails. A fainted foe, or an invalid slot, leads to getRandomTarget. With activePerHalf 2 that falls to side.randomFoe() = sample(live foes), and the move never auto-retargets to the ally. getActionSpeed also calls getTarget (for priority modifiers), so an invalid chosen slot can cause the same random draw during every queue re-sort.
mechanics.rng_draws: sample(foes), which is random(n), when retargeting after the chosen foe faints. The draw happens even when n = 1.

mechanics.name: Golisopod weight
mechanics.behavior: weighthg = weightkg*10, set in setSpecies. Golisopod is 1080 hg and the Mega is 1480 hg. getWeight = max(1, ModifyWeight(weighthg)) with no handlers in this matchup. The only weight-based move among the 12 sets is ally Farigiraf's Grass Knot (target 'normal', so it can target Golisopod). Its BP is 100 against both formes (>= 1000 and < 2000 hg). Grass is 1x against Bug/Water and 0.25x against Bug/Steel. There is no Low Kick, Heavy Slam or Heat Crash on either team.

mechanics.name: Golisopod speed and action order
mechanics.behavior: Spe is 61 in both formes (Mega keeps base 40). Champions getActionSpeed = getStat('spe') with boosts and modifiers, negated under Trick Room. There is no 10000-speed flip and no 13-bit truncation. Paralysis gives floor(61*50/100) = 30. Speeds I computed for all 12 sets: Grimmsnarl 72, Farigiraf 80, Politoed 94, Milotic 101, Ceruledge 106, Rillaboom 113, Archaludon 114, Gholdengo 118, Charizard and Mega Charizard Y 163, Staraptor 167 (Mega 178), Raichu 178 (Mega Y 200). Golisopod is therefore strictly the slowest, with no base tie. It moves last among priority-0 actions, and first under ally Farigiraf's Trick Room. Team A's Tailwind only doubles Team A. Actions are sorted by comparePriority (order, priority, speed, subOrder, effectOrder), and speeds are refreshed and the queue re-sorted after every action in gen >= 8.
mechanics.champions_override: getActionSpeed: -speed under Trick Room, instead of trunc(10000 - speed, 13).
